en: When Bodhidharma came from the West, he said, "I do not establish written words. Yet, even this was already an establishment.

Consequently, for a thousand years thereafter, these teachings have been piled as high as mountains and accumulated like peaks wherever they go. As the accumulations have become so vast, those who read them have grown weary and satiated.
This present record is precisely a selection of one or two items from among that which has caused such weariness; it is like the vernal splendor of the Shanglin Park captured in a single painting.
As for these two flowers, how could one wait until they have withered and their crimson and purple hues have faded before knowing the vast expanse of the springtime?

Once one knows spring, it is permissible to call this record "establishing words," and it is also permissible to call it "not establishing words. In either case, neither has anything to do with the matter at hand.
Preface by Huisi (Shi Ming) of Gushan on the Buddha’s Day of Enlightenment in the Wuxu Year.

Preface to the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Huizhao of Linji in Tianzhen Prefecture.
By Yan Kang Dian Xueshi, Jinguang Zhaolu Dafu, and Anfu Shi of Zhending Fu Road.
Simultaneously serving as Commander-in-Chief of the Cavalry and Infantry and concurrently presiding over the administration of Chengde Commandery.
At Huangbo Mountain, he was struck by a severe blow of the staff; only beneath Dayu’s ribs did he finally understand the meaning of the fist. An old woman with too much talk.
This bed-wetting ghost-child, this wind-crazed fellow! To stroke the tiger’s whiskers once again; to plant pines in a rocky valley—merely a pretext for later generations.
With his spade he digs the earth, nearly burying himself alive. Would he ever acknowledge such a young upstart? He slaps his own mouth and departs, burning the desk and its contents.
Severing the tongue in its tracks—neither Henan nor Hebei—one returns to the north. Facing an ancient ferry crossing, one ferries those coming and going;

holding fast to the critical ford, standing like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high. Seizing both person and environment, he molds and refines the *siddhas*; through the Three Essentials and Three Mysteries, he brings all to completion.
The hammering of the patch-robed monk is ever within the household, never departing from the path. The true person of no rank enters and exits through the gateway of the face.

When both halls shout in unison, guest and host are clearly distinguished. Illumination and function are simultaneous; fundamentally there is no before or after. It is like a rhinoceros horn facing its reflection.
The sound was transmitted from Xugu; his wondrous response knew no bounds. Leaving no trace behind, he brushed off his robes and journeyed south.

Arriving in Daming, he inherited the lineage of Master Xinghua. Welcomed at Dongtang, he attended him there. With copper pitcher and iron bowl, he shut his room and silenced his words. The pines grew old and the clouds were idle.
Vast and open, he was at ease with himself. Not long after facing the wall, as his end drew near, he secretly entrusted [the Dharma], asking:
"Who shall transmit the True Dharma? It shall perish with the blind donkey; Old Yuanjue shall propagate it. Now, for the sake of its circulation, I have examined it and found it free of error.

Only one shout remains, which still requires deliberation. May those of the Chan school who possess the eye not fail in their transmission. Written on the Mid-Autumn Day of the Gengzi year of the Xuanhe era.
Respectfully preface.
The Words of Chan Master Shanzhao of Fenyang. The successor of Shishan asked Shishan:
"What was the meaning behind Baizhang rolling up his sitting mat? Shishan said: "The dragon’s sleeve is swept aside, revealing its entire body."
Xian asked, "I do not yet understand what the Master’s meaning is. Shanshan said, "Where the Elephant King walks, the tracks of foxes are cut off. Thereupon, the Master attained realization.
Rising from his prostrations, he said: "The moon in the empty expanse of the ten-thousand-year-old azure pool—only after repeated scooping and searching does one finally come to know it."
Someone asked, "What principle did you perceive that led you to accept [the Way] for yourself? The Master said, "This is precisely where I let go of my body and life.
A monk asked, "What is the source of the Great Way? The Master said, "Digging into the earth to seek the blue sky.
"How is it the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "A fan of green silk provides enough wind and coolness. The Master then said, "The Gate of Fenyang..."
Below, there is a lion from the West River who sits crouching at the gate; as soon as anyone approaches, he bites them to death.
What skillful means is there by which one might enter the gate of Fenyang and see the person of Fenyang? If you see the person of Fenyang, you are fit to be a teacher to the patriarchs and Buddhas;
if you do not see the person of Fenyang, you are all just people standing here dead. Is there anyone present now [who can do so]?
"Have you entered the gate? You must enter quickly, lest you bring your entire life to naught. If you are not a guest of the Dragon Gate, take care not to suffer the 'dotted forehead' (rejection).
But for those who are guests of the Dragon Gate, they are all marked at once. [He raises his staff and] says, "Withdraw quickly!
Withdraw quickly! Be careful!"

Heaven and earth are vast and expansive; the universe is spread out wide. Within the sphere of the patch-robed monk, there are openings to the left and right. The woodcutter carries his firewood; the King of Physicians appraises its value.
Medicine is abundant while the illness is grave; the net is fine while the fish are dense. East, west, south, and north, they charge through frost and trample through snow.
Disregarding cold and heat, one must clarify this matter; it requires a person capable of cutting through with a single stroke to achieve it.
Merely remaining in such a state of dithering and hesitation, like a rotting winter melon—what accomplishment can there be? Even "biting through both ends" is still muddying the waters;
how much more so to remain complacent! Alas for you, brothers; the True Dharma is difficult to hear.
The True Eye is difficult to awaken. Why do you not examine yourself? It is like two armies meeting;
if one does not yield the first move, one must seize the drum and capture the banner with swift decisiveness. Every person is resolute, each one a hero.
You who are great men, do not let your practice fall into neglect, nor let the offerings of the faithful go to waste. The mountain clouds are vast and wide—when will they ever cease? If not...
With one's own wisdom penetrating the profound mysteries, one should simply settle accounts for past karmic debts. Why do you trouble yourself with such restless wandering to deceive your parents?

Having already lived this life in vain, you go further to leave the household life and travel on foot, saying, "I am visiting spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) to see my nature and cut off the flow of birth and death, realizing the unconditioned Dharma.
Alas, alas! Out of ten thousand, not one reflects upon returning to the root.

Indeed. One who expounds the Dharma must possess the eye of a master; they must recognize the gate of mystery (*xuánmén*). They must discern between the black and the white, the heterodox and the orthodox.
An ancient said: "The mysterious has its own path; the bird-path is difficult to traverse. A single word that is not mysterious belongs to a worldly teacher. Furthermore—
He asked the elders, "What is this mysterious path? Do you understand? Let me explain it to you, Fenyang.
If you wish to know the ultimate point, do not merely pass your time in such a state of dull stagnation, wasting the offerings of the faithful.
Since the time of the ancient worthies, each has had a way to transcend; have you reflected upon this? The former sages said: 'A single phrase must embody the three mysteries.'"

The Single Mysterious Gate must be complete with its Three Essentials. Which one is that phrase of the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials? Understand it well! Each of you should reflect for yourselves:

have you attained a state of stability yet? When the ancients of old traveled as pilgrims, if they heard a single kōan (in-yuan) they did not understand, they would immediately lose their appetite for food and find no peace in sleep; they would press forward with urgency to resolve it.
Do not regard this as a minor matter. This is why the Great Awakened Elder appeared in the world for the sake of the "one great cause.
Consider that from the past until now, those who have traveled on pilgrimage have not done so to sightsee among mountains and waters, nor to view the splendors of prefectures and capitals.
Wearing but a single robe and subsisting on alms-food, all this was because my holy mind had not yet attained penetration.

Therefore, I traveled far and wide on foot to investigate and resolve the profound mysteries, to transmit and propagate the teachings by consulting those who possessed prior knowledge and drawing near to those of high virtue.

This was done to continue the lamp of the Buddha’s mind, to perpetuate the legacy of the patriarchs, to exalt the sacred lineage, and to guide future seekers. Thus, for the sake of self-benefit and the benefit of others, I have never forgotten the traces left by my predecessors, as I do now.
"Is there anyone who wishes to deliberate? If so, come forward. Let us deliberate together. A monk asked, "What is the phrase for receiving a beginner?
The Master said, "Are you a wandering monk? The monk asked, "What is the phrase for discerning a patch-robed monk? The Master said, [as before].
The Master said: "The sun rises in the west at the hour of Mao. What is the phrase for when the true command is being exercised? The Master said:
"Bringing it from a thousand miles away to present one's original face. "What is the phrase for establishing heaven and earth? The Master said:

"In the continent of Uttarakuru, long-grained rice grows; those who eat it have neither greed nor anger. The Master said: "Use these four turning phrases alone to test the patch-robed monks of the world."
The monk said, "As soon as I saw you come out, I verified it. "How is it that this student exerts effort?
The Master said, "At Jia Prefecture, they strike the Great Image. "How is it that this student turns his body? The Master said, "In Shan Prefecture, they water the Iron Ox.
"How is it that this student reaches the intimate point? The Master said, "The Lion of West River. The Master said, "If a person can discern..."
Having attained these three phrases, you have already harmonized the Three Mysteries (Sanxuan). Yet there remains the language of the Three Essentials (Sanyao);
you must realize it thoroughly, for it is no ordinary matter. I shall offer a verse for the assembly: The Three Mysteries and Three Essentials are difficult to distinguish;

When the meaning is grasped, the Way is easy to approach. A single phrase clearly encompasses the myriad phenomena; On the Double-Ninth Festival, the chrysanthemums are fresh. The Master asked: "Do you understand? If so..."
"How do you understand this? You are not yet a monk of fiery temperament. How should you understand it? Long standing, take care.
The early morning assembly said: "At dawn, at the hour of Yin (3–5 am), within the state of delusion lies the person of the Way. All of you have come up here upon hearing the sound of the bell."
This is not a wild mechanism. Which one is the person of the Way? Is there anyone who can recognize it?
If you recognize it now, you will never again be deceived by it until the end of the future. If you do not recognize it, frogs and earthworms will mock you.
To speak of it a thousand times or ten thousand times is not as good as seeing it for oneself.

If you see it clearly for yourself, you will immediately transcend the mundane and enter the sacred, no longer being deluded or disturbed by the various māras. This is called "the great matter already resolved.
However, whenever anyone comes before you, not a single artifice can be employed. Therefore, Zhaozhou said: "This old monk simply watches this; it is not [something else]."
This eye for discerning dharmas—what the World-Honored One Śākyamuni called the "wondrously luminous true nature"—requires no artificial adornment.

If you can grasp it, you will avoid falsely identifying with external conditions and wasting your time in vain. A monk asked, "What is the guest within the guest? The Master said, "Joining palms before the hut, he asks the World-Honored One.
"What is the host within the guest? The Master said, "Facing one another, there is no person; it is dark. "How is it? [The monk asked. The Master said, "..."
"This is the guest within the host. The Master said: "The battle clouds stretch across the sea; drawing the sword, he stirs the Dragon Gate. [The student] asked:
"What is the host within the host? The Master said: "With three heads and six arms, he supports heaven and earth; the wrathful Nātha strikes down the Imperial Bell."
The Master then said: "The elders of all quarters, having no other recourse, speak here and there.
You all imagine that it should be thus, elaborating explanations at length and each vying to huddle together, saying you will not sleep or rest while seeking the Way.
But where do you intend to seek? An ancient said: 'To apply effort toward the external is to be nothing but a foolish and stubborn fellow. You must act quickly."
"Believe and accept this; do not stand for long.
After the first yang-line arises, the days grow by one thread each day. Tell me, how much does the Buddha-dharma grow?
While the Master was seated in the abbot’s quarters with monks and laypeople standing in attendance, a person entered whose name and origin were unknown.
He prostrated and, rising, asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "My house is vast; there is no seed that is not present.
The student said, "I have not yet understood the Master’s profound meaning. I beg the Master for a skillful means to display the sharp edge of the encounter.
The Master said, "The lion’s seat is settled within the abbot’s quarters; the dragon-shaped staff is held in my hand. The student asked, "As for one who uses it, how is it? The Master said, "Zhi."
He shattered the stone of stubborn ignorance and gathered the treasure of the illuminating star. [The student] asked, "What is the treasure of the illuminating star?

The Master said, "I am walking through the wild weeds; you, moreover, have entered a deep village. The man prostrated himself, then rose and went out the door, immediately disappearing and no longer to be found.
[The Master] picked up his staff and said, "If you recognize this, your studies are complete. Do you recognize it? Do not say, 'What do you call this?
Such people as these are like dust and sand; I allow you to deliberate, but how will you open your mouth?
Try to say something. A monk asked, "What is the staff? The Master said, "Deshan, Deshan. The monk said, "I have understood. The Master said, "Wrong!"
"In what place? The Master said, "Svāhā. The Master then said, "Is there anything more you wish to ask? Ask quickly!

A site of practice (doctrinal field) is difficult to encounter, and time passes swiftly. With a single breath gone, it is ten thousand kalpas in the Yellow Springs (the realm of death). I have stood for a long time; take care and bid me farewell."
The sound of the bell and the chirping of sparrows can accord with the true source; to seek elsewhere is to give rise to delusive complications.

To believe that one can kindle fire by blowing on the wind is to trust in the impossible, while not believing that one must dig a pit on level ground is to ignore reality. Having no choice but to act, one begins to model and paint patterns.
Thus it is said: "On Vulture Peak they spoke of the moon; at Caoxi they pointed to the moon. Where is the moon? Point it out to me! Directly report this to Chan.
Harmony. Do not seek it in the heavens. A monk asked, "What is the moon that does not reside in the heavens?
The Master said, "Illumination. The Master said: "Clearly knowing there is not a single thing, why use further seeking? At this very place, do not insist on giving it a name."
Where is there any sharp edge? To grasp it directly—even that is but a broken bow and a shattered arrow; what use could it have?
If you hesitate or deliberate, you are merely a broom for clearing the battlefield. With his staff, he struck them all down at once.

Zheng Gongbu, the Commissioner of Transport for Hedong, entered the mountains to visit him. During their conversation over tea, the Commissioner said, "I have specifically prepared a verse to present to you, Master.
May I do so? The Master replied, "How could I dare? The Commissioner was kind enough to compose a verse on the wall in seal script, which read:
"Do not let yellow paper obscure your eyes; The blue clouds naturally provide shade. Do not bury the Patriarch’s legacy With the intellectual learning of the mundane."
The Master said, "I will take this verse and test the elders throughout the land. Fengbo said, "In that case, even Fenyang would be included among them.
The Master said, "Carrying the cangue, you pass the indictment. Fengbo said, "There is no further interrogation. The Master said, "If you know, then you have it.
After Fengbo had been silent for a long while, the Master let out a single sigh. Fengbo said, "Wenbao! Wenbao!"
The Master said, "Where exactly? The Official said, "I cannot allow you to vent your spleen alone; how could I fail to resent him saying that the Elder has been detained here for so long?
The Master said, "What kind of talk is this? The Official said, "It is true. The Master said, "In that case, you may not let him go unpunished."
Fobu said, "I beg the Master for a verse; would it be possible? The Master said, "I am not practiced in literary composition. Fobu said, "I beg the Master to dictate it orally.
The Master then said: "Through the weeds, one toils to find the path; The rocky pines spread their shade afar. How many seekers of the profound mystery Have lost their original mind!"
The Goose King selects milk; he has never been of the duck species. A monk asked: "The Goose King selects milk; he has never been of the duck species—what is the meaning of this?
The Master said: "There is [milk] in Jiangnan, but none in Jiangbei. The Master said: "With so much entanglement, can you still understand?
You have not yet grasped it clearly; keep the question in mind. You must immediately investigate and examine the principle through inquiry. It is not [found] in Fusang."
Far away! Do not run outward in pursuit. It arises where you are; it manifests spontaneously wherever you are. The heavens, the earth, and the great world are bright and clear.
Simply, throughout the twelve periods of the day, while walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, contemplate carefully:

who is creating this obstacle? Why is it that when facing a critical moment, you are unable to speak? It is simply because all sensory objects and consciousnesses are obstructed; you are being held back by them.

It turns back and exchanges; it then follows after objects and wanders, unable to exercise mastery. Therefore, within a single phrase, the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials, and the four types of guest and host, are all clearly present.
It is only because the clouds of afflictions from many lifetimes have obscured [the mind] that one has been cast away in this life.
Furthermore, you have not approached an enlightened teacher to seek decisive discernment. Do not let the days pass by in vain. As the ancients said: "Now..."
Birth is not unobstructed; the coming life is constricted and blocked, becoming increasingly obscure. To engage in mere deliberation is to vainly prolong the years and months, wasting one’s time.

Whether layperson or renunciant, you must simply bring this to realization. If you can realize it, then until the end of the future, throughout the heavens and the human realm, you shall let out the lion’s roar, proclaiming it to humans and devas, acting as host and guest to one another with sovereign mastery over expansion and contraction, serving as a refuge and a support.
Cease! To take this as the Way or the Path is a profound obstacle. If you do not understand clearly, there will be a thousand difficulties and ten thousand hardships.
You must quickly realize it; cast off the sense-bases and their objects. If you fail to understand, it is in vain to speak of "the present. Take care!
A monk asked, "I bring this raw jade to you, Master; I pray you, polish it for me. The Master said, "Bring it again tomorrow morning to show the King of Chu.
To seek instruction morning and evening is merely the ordinary course of things. Since it does not fall within the realm of verbal explanation, how would you express it?
Holding up his staff, he said: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time are all here. Look!

Seeing that you have no openings, they have all entered into this staff and are vainly producing knots and joints. Is there anyone who can catch them? If there is, take a step forward and try to catch them!
A monk stepped forward, and the Master said: "In a mere flash, they have already been cast thousands of miles away. He struck him again and said: "I..."
Already you have leaped into a pit of mud; why do you wait any longer to add straw to the flames?
You are like such a master—will you even be saved? The monk bowed. The Master said, "Come, come! Do you understand this tangle? The monk said, "I do not.
The Master said, "It is fortunate that you do not. Fenyang found his mouth to eat his rice: *sulu sulu*."
The Master, while contemplating the words of the Five Ranks spoken by Master Dongshan Liangjie, composed this verse: "The five ranks must be understood with utmost care;
The slightest movement already constitutes a deviation. Who can wield the diamond sword within its scabbard? Only Nanda possesses the foremost faculty.
A single glance brings the three realms to stillness; Shaking the bell causes the nine heavens to return. Within the very center is the subtle..."
The hero’s way is one of mutual penetration; if you deliberate upon it, you lose its sharp edge and its majesty.
A monk asked, "What is coming from the center? The Master said, "Dried-up land lotuses bloom flower after flower. The monk asked, "What is it like after they have bloomed?

The Master said, "Golden stamens and silver filaments receive the jade dew; the eminent monk does not sit upon the phoenix terrace. "What is being off-center within the center? The Master said, "The jade hare..."
Once the first watch of the night has passed, the golden rooster must announce the fifth watch. What is "correctness within partiality"?
The Master said: "A mere hair grows into a great tree; a drop of water becomes a river. What is "arrival through integration"? The Master said:
"One's spirit and will are not obtained from Heaven and Earth; how could a hero rely on the shifting of the four seasons? What is "reaching through integration"? The Master said:
The jade maiden throws the shuttle with a whirring sound; the stone man beats the drum with a thumping resonance.
A monk asked, "What was it like before Niutou had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "The shaman must further offer a sacrifice to the shamaness."
To see what happens next: An ancient temple has once again been inscribed by a scholar. The Master then said: "Hearing sounds and seeing forms, light radiates wherever the eye falls;
mountains are high and seas are vast, earth is enduring and heaven is eternal. How do you discern the Lord of Lords?"

The regions of Bing and Fen were bitterly cold, so he consequently discontinued the evening assemblies. A strange monk arrived, shaking his mendicant’s staff, and said, "There are six great beings (mahāsattvas) within this assembly;
for what reason do you not preach the Dharma? Having spoken, he departed. The Master secretly recorded this in a verse:
"The foreign monk with the golden staff’s radiance Has come to Fenyang for the sake of the Dharma. Six persons are vessels for the Law; I entreat you to proclaim it for them."
The Master said to the assembly: "Now, one who preaches the Dharma must possess the ten knowledges that accord with reality.

If one does not possess these ten knowledges that accord with reality, they will fail to distinguish between the heterodox and the orthodox, and will be unable to differentiate between the ordained and the laity. Such a person cannot serve as eyes for gods and humans to determine right from wrong.
They would be like a bird flying through the sky with broken wings, or like an arrow shot at a target with a severed string; because the string is severed, the arrow misses the target."
It will not hit. Because the wing is broken, the arrow cannot fly through the air. When the string is strong and the wing is firm, the arrow and the target both penetrate each other.

What is it that constitutes the "Ten Wisdoms Identical with Reality"? I shall point them out for you, Senior Monk: 1. Identical in substance; 2. Identical in the Great Matter; 3. Identical in being fellow practitioners;
4. Identical in true resolve; 5. Identical in universal pervasiveness; 6. Identical in complete fulfillment; 7. Identical in gain and loss; 8. [The eighth...]
1. Identical in birth and killing. 2. Nine: identical in the sound of the roar. 3. Ten: identical in attaining entry. It is further asked:
With what person is one identical in attaining entry? With whom is one identical in the sound of the roar? What is this identical birth and killing? What thing is identical in gain and loss?
Which one is identical in being fully endowed? What is identical in its universal pervasiveness? Who is identical in true resolve? Who is able to be entirely identical?
"Param! Which one is the same as the Great Matter? What thing shares the same substance? Is there anyone who can point it out?
To those who can point it out, I shall not begrudge my compassion. If you cannot point it out, you do not yet possess the eye of study.
You must discern this; you must recognize right from wrong. The true face is already present before you; do not stand here for long."
Two Verses for the Assembly: The lightning-fast pivot of the enlightened mind is not easily met; To attempt to grasp it with the calculating intellect leads only to madness.

Even if you could bite down on an arrowhead flying at you, It would still be like a tortoise hiding within the water. A swift flame passing through the wind is even more difficult to engage; A raised brow or a blink of an eye separates one by a thousand mountains.
To hesitate over rushing waters or crossing a blade is already a stagnation; To deliberate upon it is like— (Note: The text appears to break off mid-verse.)
How can anything further be preserved?
Both sudden and gradual approaches are encompassed. To see one's nature is to transcend words and letters;
in the mind that studies and recognizes, the mind itself is the Buddha. Not recognizing it is the Demon King. Demon and Buddha are made from one mind: the Buddha is true, while the demon is deluded.
Seeing one's nature is beyond words; what need is there for the texts of a thousand ocean-treasuries? When the mind is raised, the meaning is clear; it does not lie in extensive verbosity.
How many from former studies could truly know this? Picking up pebbles from the mud, those who can discern jewels are rare.
Only those of hidden, lofty aspirations remain carefree and unburdened, blending with the times.
The Words of Master Langya Huijue Ascending the hall as the successor of Fenyang, he held up his staff and said:
"Sometimes this mountain monk’s single blow brings forth the birth of all Buddhas;
sometimes this single blow turns the Great Dharma Wheel; sometimes this single blow enters parinirvāṇa. Now tell me: when the Buddhas are born..."
"The turning of the Great Dharma Wheel and the entry into Parinirvāṇa—how much time lies between them? After a long silence, he said, "Do not slander the Tathāgata’s True Dharma Wheel. Take care."
The Master cited the former Liangshan, who said: "To those coming from the south, I give thirty blows; to those coming from the north, I give thirty blows.
Although it was thus, he did not hit the mark of the school. The Master said: "Liangshan had a piece of fine gold, yet he sold it as dull iron.
Lingya is not like this: to those coming from the south, I give thirty blows; to those coming from the north, I give thirty blows."
"Ten blows! Let the monks of the world under heaven criticize as they will.
Be careful! [The Master] raised a case: A monk asked Great Master Ma, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "This very mind is the Buddha.
[The monk asked,] "What is the Way? [The Master] said, "No-mind is the Way. [The monk asked,] "How far apart are the Buddha and the Way? The Master said, "The Buddha is like unfolding..."

[The Master] held up his hand; it appeared as if he were clenching a fist. The Master said, "The expedient means of the ancients are not to be dismissed, yet here in my place there is also a bit of something.
If no one buys it, I shall sell it myself. "What is the Buddha? "Before the cliff, many auspicious herbs grow. "What is the Way?
"At the bottom of the ravine, spiritual sprouts abound. "How far apart are the Buddha and the Way? "Not even a hair's breadth."

A single white cloud enshrouds the ancient temple; a ribbon of green water winds around the blue mountains. Take care. For one who comes in this manner, they are assigned to the upper chamber. For one who does not come in this manner, they hang their robe at the lower level. When a person of the highest caliber arrives, they cross the river alone in silent sorrow. Where, then, shall another person be placed? After a long silence, he said: [The Master] struck the meditation seat once. He then said: "If you can speak a word here, you may go to the upper chamber. If you cannot, you must go to the lower level. A monk stepped forward and asked, "What about one who has neither come nor gone? The Master said, "He is already on the path.
