At that time, the heavens rained down *māndārava* flowers and *mahāmāndārava* flowers. O Great Assembly, at first, the World-Honored One seemed almost as if he were indifferent to all others.
Today, although this mountain monk is indeed like a child who cannot equal his father, I too shall not enter into immeasurable [samādhi].
"Samādhi! For now, let us avoid the heavens raining the four flowers. He then picked up his staff and said, "I shall turn the Great Dharma Wheel for you all.
He struck the ground with the staff and descended from the seat.
The Buddhas appear in the world to prescribe remedies according to the ailments; yet when the Patriarchs came from the West, they were like those who wait by a stump for a rabbit.

Even if one were to fully uphold and proclaim the teachings, it would be like boring through a wall to steal a glimmer of light; even if one were to implement them all, it would be much like casting a sword into the air.
Why is this? Have you not seen the ancients say: "One need not seek the Truth; one must only cease [conceptual] views"? Gentlemen, tell me:
what kind of view is it that must be ceased? After a long silence, he said: "If Lingyun had not awakened to the meaning of the peach blossoms, Xuansha would have been forced to frown in vain."
A wind blows once every three days; it rains once every five days. As for Deshan and Linji, there is no need to cite them further.

Consider this monk’s question to Caoshan: “How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? Caoshan replied, “Caoshan is not as good. The monk asked again, “How was it after he appeared in the world?

Furthermore, you must know that atop the peak of Mount Miaofeng there is one person who utterly refuses to accept Caoshan speaking in such a manner.
Do you all recognize this person? If you do not, I, this mountain monk, shall reveal him for your sake. After a long silence, he said:
"It would be better to cut out one's tongue than to violate the imperial taboo."
The ancients said: "To cling to phenomena is fundamentally delusion; to accord with principle is likewise not awakening. How can one avoid this? After a long silence, he said:

The Shaoshi Peak stands empty and closed; whose fault is this? It is like planting oaks to await the phoenix or sowing bamboo to invite the wind.

Had it not been for the Second Patriarch who took up the succession, the green mountains would still have remained as they were, draped in their azure hues. "Virtuous ones, tell me: what was it that he inherited?

Small Assembly:

A single phrase: how could the Patriarch Buddha have known this? A special ox gives birth to a calf in these present times. A single melody in the dark is faintly recognizable;
a lamp illuminating fragmentary texts is no poem.

thereby enabling him to recognize his own school (2).

When the Buddhas and Patriarchs speak, their path becomes increasingly divergent; the stone man’s discourse is quite harmonious. In vain do they employ blows and shouts to hasten the gate’s proceedings;

Amidst death, life is found;

in the ultimate state, the profound mechanism is free from right and wrong. When spring arrives early in Jiangnan, the partridges cry; all say that by manifesting the mind through form, one realizes it.

A living bird that is already dead carries a flower to fall before the green cliffs. Facing all objects, everyone says it is transmitted everywhere. When people ask about the West, he points to the courtyard.
Cypress—how could it concern the verdant hues piercing the mountain peaks?

The heron; the fisherman dances his oars and pushes through the mist as he returns home.
When the hundred negations are abandoned and the myriad delusions are eliminated, there is no mind facing objects—every thing is the Way. Within the realm of true purity, it takes but a single...

How can there be any difference between not abandoning the true gold and entering the fire? The utpala flower blooms within the flames; who could create it amidst the path of afflictions?
Companion. Within the ocean of ignorance, one sinks and floats of one's own accord.

Long. The crescent moon’s curved form is often clear;
the drawn sword that severs life, its poised momentum is inexhaustible. From this point on, both sages and commoners forever lose their traces. The Ba River is swift and vast; few can cross it.

In ordinary times, a week passes before the spring breeze returns. At the wild crossing by the riverbank, the fishing old man stirs. Along the embankment, green willows mingle with the rain.

On the sharp path, uprooting birth—do not look for lost gold coins among the yellow leaves. This is simply it; how could there be "before" or "after"? A bottomless treasury transmitted by the thousand sages.

he has transcended the fresh green branches by the Yellow Crane Tower. Between the two waters and three mountains, the scenery spreads wide; in the southern lands, miasma and heat are abundant.

Whether one penetrates through or not, between the eastern mountains and western ridges, there is red and green. It is said that there is a gate for responding with words; one must leap over the southern mounds and northern hills.

Verse: The cowherd boy holds his flute horizontally and again dons his rain cape.

Fresh green grass begins to sprout as tender bamboo is broken; wild birds flit about in confusion as the mountain stream divides its course. Mist on the ridges has just begun to clear, yet the clouds remain pale;
a sliver of light illuminates the outskirts, while the trees still do not conceal the ground.
The landscape is seized but the man is not;
the wind and snow at Lan Pass make the path impassable. At the wild crossing, he seeks a boat to visit the fishing old man. Five li of distant longing, then another five;
one night of sorrow shared with another.
Both person and environment are utterly swept away:
on the stone path, spring returns but the grass is not green. The desolate ruins and level plains have the moon as their neighbor; where the mountains of Chu are severed, scattered clouds disperse;
the waters of the Wei River run dry and the trees of Qin fall.

the breeze blows through the valleys where new green moss grows. The flowing waters gush forth, threading through Mengjin; the orioles warble in Shanglin Park, filling the imperial capital with sound.

Recalling the past, where could even a single dharma come from that is not born? Wandering into delusion, a thousand words only lead further astray into error.

I rejoice now that I may receive the lingering grace of my predecessors and return to true awakening. I bid a high farewell to the King of Emptiness and contemplate this mind. Simply let daily life proceed with a peaceful and steady heart;
then the emotional dust of Buddhas and Patriarchs will naturally subside.
When this white ox was first brought out into the open, I was too weary to lead him; I feared his branching horns would trample the people’s fields.

Yet the cypress stairs remain as before, stretching long with verdant shade.

where have the people of past and present gone? The waters divide their heads and come bearing the moon.

Amidst white clouds at midnight, I embrace the rocky crags; as the moon rises over a thousand peaks, the green ridges glow at dawn.

It reaches the point where all is merged into a single color, vast and boundless, difficult to distinguish. Yet even when examined closely, this remains but the talk of the present age.

He is able to discourse on the essentials of the Dharma. The lantern leans its ear; the pillar nods its head. If you can realize this here and now, you will find lifelong joy and fulfillment.

Do not harbor self-doubt or despondency, nor go further to question Buddhas or patriarchs, speaking of the Way or of Chan; for I fear this would only bury you. Do you understand? Truly.
Jiuyun said, "It has already fallen into the second month," and then descended from his seat.

"One may know only that the jade of Jing is different; how can one discern the heart of the King of Chu?"
Before the time of Bhīṣmagarjitasvarakalpa, there was no falling into various stages; after the time of Dīpaṃkara, mind was transmitted through mind.

The various patriarchs successively inherited this lineage. The "closing the room" at Magadha seems right yet is not; furthermore, in the Deer Park, he turned the Wheel of Dharma in three phases and twelve aspects.

"I have the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye, which I entrust to you. Yet the golden-colored *dhūta* was truly no gentleman, merely accepting another’s decree.

Today, I cannot help but follow the error with the error, bending my ways for the sake of these times. From the beginning I have told you: you must clarify the Source beyond the ultimate meaning;
do not seek the standard within words. Even a stone man like you would understand how to sing a folk song; if you were like a stone man, [the snow]...

Yet it has fallen into the present moment. But tell me, how would you speak of that which has not yet transcended the world?
After a long silence, he said: "Realize it before the first signs of manifestation have arisen. The spring breeze stirs, and the green willows hang down."
Beyond the Way of Majestic Sound (Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja), where a thousand sages have never traveled, words of question and answer are like a journey of ten thousand miles to one’s native land.
Even if one were entirely not thus, sitting within the realm of non-action, were one to further fix the gaze, there would be no need for mutual encounter.
This morning is the first day of the fifth month. The Stone Man holds a fan of the cold heavens in his hand; rest, rest—there is no front or back.

Behold you, directly beneath it, forgetting all knowledge and views. If you rely on the path of study, when will it ever end? In a mere flash, if emotion arises, Mara finds his opportunity. Do you understand? After a long silence, he said:
"To practice the profound while embodying the subtle is to fall into a deviant path; to investigate principle and exhaust the source is a thousand miles away. Study!
Two thousand years ago, the World-Honored One had a dream while in the Tuṣita Heaven. In the dream, he saw himself descending into his mother’s womb;

Everyone, tell me: is this the same as today, or is it different? Therefore it is said: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time speak dreams;
the six ancestral patriarchs speak dreams; the old monks of the world speak dreams; and I, this mountain monk, today speak a dream. Everyone—

"Have you ever seen it in a dream? After a long silence, he said: "Were it not for the melting of the remaining ice in the Western Regions, how could one see the green eyes of the willows in the Eastern Garden?
He descended from his seat. The Dharma has no "this" or "that";
the Way has no ordinary or holy. It is ever-peaceful throughout kalpas, transcending all cultivation and realization. Those who attain it—red.

Now, let both good and evil thoughts be swept away from you all at once. Teach them directly so that where there is an end, it is not made into a home;

where there is emptiness, it is not made into a seat; and where there are myriad practices, they are not made into robes. Walking shall be like the path of a bird; sitting shall be like empty space. After a long silence, he said: "Do you understand?"

The path to entering the Way is inner emptiness and outer stillness, like water that is clear and motionless, where the myriad phenomena are reflected in light—neither sinking nor floating.
The myriad dharmas are as they are. Thus it is said: fire does not wait for the sun to be hot; wind does not wait for the moon to be cool.
Hard stones dwell in water; the blind of heaven still possess light. Brightness and darkness exist of themselves; dryness and moisture share the same direction.

If one can be thus, then withered trees before the cliff will bloom at midnight; a wooden woman carrying a basket under the clear breeze and the moon; a stone man dancing his sleeves—[all] together...
Celebrating great peace, the rustic elders sing songs of joy; those who possess true understanding find harmony herein.
If one can clearly realize this, why must one ascend a temple tower again or seek to behold Mañjuśrī once more? The Way is right before one's eyes—realize it all at once!
A single dharma universally encompasses all dharmas. Holding up his whisk, he said:

A Small Sermon for the New and Former Administrative Officers: There is advancing and there is retreating; this has been the constant custom from antiquity to the present. To advance is like a dragon returning to the vast ocean:
all species have a place to rely upon, and each finds its proper station. To retreat is like a wild goat hanging by its horns:

form and shadow are not manifest, as one nurtures the sacred embryo and gradually becomes a great vessel. These two modes—self-benefit and benefiting others—are each indispensable to the other and do not weaken one another.
Tonight, this mountain monk exhorts you all: do not study the Buddha-dharma. Should you conceive the thought of studying it, the weeds will grow ten feet deep.
All the patriarchs of the past have been buried by you in the depths of these thickets of grass. Tonight, this mountain monk shall clear their grievance for the patriarchs;
I exhort you all not to seek it within the volumes of the scriptures or upon the pages of books. Even if there were words...
Within these words, there is a point of entry. It is like the light of a firefly; it cannot save itself.

If you awaken to and clarify your own nature during the time before kalpas, it will be like hundreds of thousands of suns and moons—its radiance immeasurable, liberating boundless sentient beings all at once.
If you have not yet clarified this, you must simply take a step back and return to yourself; only then will you find rest. Rest! Rest!
Go! Rest yourself until you are at rest. Be like the incense burner in an ancient temple; let a single thought endure for ten thousand years.

Be like a person who has not breathed for a single moment. If you can maintain this state throughout your long life, yet fail to attain the fruit of the Way, then this mountain monk speaks falsely and deceives all of you, leading you to fall into hell by your own hand. I exhort you all: do not misapply your body and mind.
Discern the path ahead; do not wait until the last moment. You must exert effort yourself; no one can take your place. Be careful.

Sitting idly while consuming the monastery’s permanent endowment, I have utterly forgotten the entrustment of the former sages. Now, I wish to follow the precedent of ancient abbots and establish an agreement with all of you:
I shall no longer descend the mountain, nor attend formal meals, nor dispatch emissaries for fundraising.
Instead, whatever income this monastery’s estates produce in one year shall be divided into three hundred and sixty equal parts; each day, one part shall be taken for our use.
Do not increase or decrease the portions according to others; simply prepare rice. If the rice is insufficient, prepare porridge. If the porridge is insufficient, prepare rice gruel.
When meeting those who have newly arrived, serve only tea and soup; do not prepare any further boiled or prepared delicacies.
Establish only a single tea hall; take what you need yourself, striving to minimize external conditions so that you may devote yourself entirely to the practice of the Way.
Moreover, your livelihood is fully provided for and the scenery is never lacking: the flowers know how to smile, and the birds can sing. The wooden horse neighs forever, and the stone ox runs well.

Sounds and traces are utterly silent; news and tidings are profoundly still. All is a single flavor of desolation, with nothing toward which one may turn.
"Venerable, today as I speak of our ancestral lineage before you all, it is already not a convenient matter.

He arrived at the foot of Mount Shaoshi and sat facing a wall for nine years. When the Second Patriarch came, he stood in the snow until his arm was severed;
one could say he underwent the utmost hardships. Yet, Bodhidharma never uttered a single word, and the Second Patriarch never asked a single question.
Can you still call Bodhidharma "one who does not act for others"? Can you still call the Second Patriarch "one who does not seek a teacher"?
Is this not so? Whenever I speak of the deeds of the ancient sages, I feel as though there is no place for me to stand. I am ashamed that later generations have become so weak.
Moreover, when they are provided with the finest delicacies and offerings, they say, "I will only resolve to cultivate the Way once the four requisites are fully provided.
I fear that before they can even move their hands or feet, they will already have passed through another life and another age.

Seventeen, eighteen—already leaked away. If you do not understand, you will remain tethered like a donkey to its hitching post.
The character "yi" (以) is not formed; the character "ba" (八) is not correct. Whether there is profit or loss, one does not leave the marketplace. [The Master] picks up his staff and says:
The Son of Heaven within the realm; the General beyond the frontier. Striking the meditation seat:
on the twenty-third day of the tenth month. The weather is cold, so the warm curtain is lowered. A single sleep at dusk: from the South Sea comes the sweet jujube.
O Noble One, at times he emerges wearing a jeweled crown and draped in necklaces;
nine out of ten people are struck with fear, revile him, and flee far away, for they do not recognize him. Thereupon, he puts on soiled and tattered garments;
when he meets them, hundreds or thousands of people simultaneously praise him with joy and come to believe that the wisdom he has attained is subtle and profound.
"Most foremost! The faculties of sentient beings are dull; they are attached to pleasure and blinded by ignorance.
How can such as these be delivered? He struck the incense table once with his staff.

While residing at Dongshan, he ascended the hall and said: "Let the exchange of questions and answers cease for now; words are many, yet the Way is far. Thus, from the perspective of one who has attained thorough understanding, there is neither 'acceptable' nor 'unacceptable.
In the free and unrestrained movement of question and answer, what is right and what is wrong? The Gate of Non-duality opens, and the One Path is pure."
The ancients said: "The Way is omnipresent; it is true in every encounter. If the mind is not crooked, one's actions will naturally be upright.
The Way of Right Enlightenment is attained within the mind, not in words. Where the path of speech is cut off, the movements of the mind cease.
It is neither ancient nor modern. In this assembly today, every dharma is as it originally is; every mind is fundamentally Buddha—whether monk or layperson."
The wise and the foolish are one. To awaken is to realize that all things are of a single family; to be deluded is to encounter ten thousand distinctions and a thousand divergences.

A deviation of a hair’s breadth results in a loss of a thousand li. Thereupon, he took up his whisk and called to the assembly, saying: "One flower opens into five petals; the fruition is naturally accomplished."
People do not recognize the mani jewel; yet the Tathāgata-garbha has personally received it. Having received it, he does not guard or cherish it, but desires for all people to see it.
He throws down his staff and says: "Do you recognize it? If you recognize it, burn aloeswood incense to make offerings to all you venerable practitioners of Chan.
The bright moon illuminates the traveler at night; this is truly because it is not the business of others."
The Buddha-dharma is manifest before us; the monastics and laity stand solemnly.
On the fifth day of the eighth month, amidst the chill of autumn, there is the formless body within the body with form, and the path of non-arising upon the road of ignorance.
Master Zhigong deceives us fools and deluded ones, treating the noble as lowly. Nevertheless, I venture to ask you all: are the four elements and five aggregates [the self] now?
This body possesses form; what, then, is that person’s formless essence? He lets out a single sigh and says:
"If one wishes to repay the grace of the former sages who protected and sustained us, how could one ever do so even by grinding one's bones and crushing one's body to dust?"
One knows only today and tomorrow; one does not realize that the early autumn has passed and the late autumn is coming. All you practitioners of Chan, have you ceased [this delusion] yet?
You should cease it now. What further matter is there? Do you see? The waters of the four great oceans pour into the nostrils of each and every one of you;
Mount Sumeru protrudes from the side of your foreheads. Thirty years hence, do not fail the Cave [of the Patriarchs].

"Venerable Elder, you preach the lion’s roar with fearlessness; when the hundred beasts hear it, their brains shatter. [The Master] struck the left side of the meditation seat and said, "This is not the lion’s roar.
He then struck the right side of the meditation seat and said, "This is not the fearless preaching. If you even conceive of an intention..."
"This is a split brain! What else could it be? A pack of wild fox spirits! He lets out a shout. "At dawn, at the hour of Yin (3–5 AM):
within the state of madness lies the person of the Way. Thereupon he shouts again, saying, "This is not madness," and spits on the ground.
"It is not a mad device. If you take it to be a mad device, how could you possibly succeed? Walking, standing, sitting, and reclining; mountains, rivers, and the great earth—it is not a mad device.
But tell me, what is the body of a man of the Way? After a long silence, he said, "Each of you return to the hall and drink tea."
This matter cannot be learned, cannot be taught, and cannot be transmitted; it must be realized by the person themselves before it can be attained.
Once realized, it is perfectly so, utterly at ease, clearly and brightly manifest, and vividly distinct.
All supernatural powers and transformations are spontaneously complete within oneself, requiring no external seeking. Then, holding his staff horizontally, he said: "Holding it horizontally..."
"Moxie completes the perfect command; in the realm of Great Peace, he slays the foolish and the stubborn. He then cast down [the staff]. After a long silence, he let out a shout:
"A lion does not eat the remains of a vulture's meal; how could a swift falcon strike at a crouching hare? He unleashed the great dragon of Linji and pulled out the single glance of Yunmen.
Holding up his staff, he said: "When the dragon moves, the rain follows; the three types of grass and two types of trees [all receive it]."

The Master of Transformation said: "A renunciant śramaṇa should maintain a pure livelihood, taking alms-gathering as his right sustenance so as not to exceed moderation and thereby remain free from arrogance.
He takes the seeking of the Dharma as his right mindfulness, so as to increase wisdom and avoid stagnating in quiescence.
He then suddenly picked up his staff and said: "If you have a staff, I give you a staff; if you have no staff—"
Son! I take away your staff. This, if you can realize it, will increase your wisdom and shatter your arrogance.

It is like concealing one’s body within a blazing flame or appearing from the midst of the mud. Let the Great Compassionate Bodhisattva with a thousand hands and a thousand eyes manifest his supernatural powers as he pleases.
If you cannot realize this, there is a clear spring for you to drink from at will, and there are emerald cliffs for you to follow.
At rest—take care that the cold monkey does not howl in the deep night.

Dongshan accepted the invitation; the assembly requested a small-scale discourse (xiaocan). In the ancient cave of Xin’feng, ten thousand peaks compete to cluster together; here lies the true trace of awakening to one’s original nature.
A thousand forests compete in their clustering; it is a supreme site throughout antiquity and the present, where Buddhist practice has flourished for a long time.
Thus, in the past, Great Master Wuben occasionally proclaimed: "Only Buddha-bodhi is the true place of reliance. He then let out a shout and said: "There is still this 'going' and 'staying'!
"O Zen adepts, as for what the Great Master said—that there is still this 'going' and 'staying'—how is it so?"
Now tell me: what is your intention? Do you know where this falls? Within the monastic communities, there are many who debate this.
Some say that hearing the Buddha or hearing the Dharma is like giving birth to an enemy; how much more so when there is still something else to rely upon?
For this reason, they were scrutinized by Master Wuben. Others say that Wuben simply wants people to find rest. Still others say that Wuben...
One sees only the sharpness of the chisel’s point; one does not see the squareness of the chisel’s head.
To match it in such a manner—how could you have even dreamed of those ancients? Since it is not like this, then how is it? Venerable ones, this matter requires the utmost care and attention.

One must not be coarse-minded. First, practice *chan* meditation and exhaustively investigate the teachings to their ultimate depths. Within the School of the Patriarchs (*zongmen*), there are a thousand differences and ten thousand distinctions;
the paths of concealment and manifestation diverge, and only those of great wisdom can clearly discern them. From this point downward, one cannot fathom their limits.
Nowadays, most people merely embrace a child who will not cry, beat a clean ball, moor a boat by casting a line, or wash themselves while clinging to a bridge—each doing so for their own sake.
"O worthy one! Who would not have a share in this? If you depart with clear understanding, you will drive away the oxen of the plowmen and snatch the food from the mouths of the hungry.
Entering fire, you shall not be burned; entering water, you shall not be drowned. You shall leave no trace in any place, yet achieve perfection everywhere.
Your numinous light shines alone, its brilliance surpassing all distinctions. One may truly say it is vast and expansive! Raise the sail to cross the river."
Plying the ferryboat to deliver others, amidst the white-capped waves within the sea of birth and death, he emerges and submerges, coming and going with ease and sovereignty.
He lets out a shout and says: "Let them slander me; let them criticize me. Amid the rain, I wear my bamboo hat and raincoat.
Now, for a time, I bid farewell to the moon at Haimen; carrying my fish, I shall return to the marketplace."

[The Master] cites the three sages and Xinghua. When encountering people, one [of them] would come out, while the other would not. The Master picks this up and says: "Look at these two ancient fellows!
They stole a mere fraction of Linji’s livelihood and each established their own boundaries and domains, their vital energy piercing the universe.
This makes even an eye-opening monk nothing but laughable. "O Zen practitioners, tell me: what is there to laugh at? Do you know where it falls?"
How is it? If you know, go ahead and act however you please, even if it is sevenfold or eightfold topsy-turvy. If you do not know, for now, chew upon the tangled vines of Sansheng and Xinghua.

At the summer retreat, the ten directions assemble; once every three months they convene to stifle the mind of wildness and arrogance, to eliminate the fever of suffering and affliction, and to attain excellence.
Cool and refreshing; they realize great nirvana and reach the further shore, leaving behind the tracks of birth and death. Because this sacred regulation exists, it is not established in vain.
Śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas neither see nor hear it; the Buddhas of the three periods can only know it for themselves.
Monks cannot leap out of it; they are caught within its intricate patterns. To move is to open one's eyes and urinate on the bed—to speak dreams within a dream. For now, turn toward...
Under the gate of Dongshan, one must seek a way to live for ninety days;

the two words "Buddha-dharma" are truly difficult to encounter. Some do not believe in their own Buddha-work, relying instead on a mere shadow of the ancients, a semblance of prajñā, the realm of what is known, or the dharma-gates of fixed characteristics. To move [in this way] is to turn one's back.
Awakening clings to the sense objects; it is stuck and cannot be released. If students come [to such teachers], it is like using a seal to stamp clay—they merely transmit one another's impressions.
Not only do they deceive themselves, but they also deceive others. Under Dongshan’s gate, there is no Buddha-dharma to give to people;
there is only a single sword. To every person who comes, he cuts them off completely, so that their very life-force does not remain, and both seeing and hearing are extinguished.
Ming. "I shall instead go back to the time before one's parents were born and meet him there. As soon as he steps forward, I shall cut him off.
Now, although a sharp sword is keen, it does not slay those who are innocent. Is there anyone who is innocent?
He also deserves thirty blows of the staff.

When Danxia burned the wooden Buddha, the abbot’s eyebrows and beard fell off. [The Master] suddenly brandishes the staff and says, "This is not a wooden Buddha," then throws it down and says, "Who dares to burn you?
If one intends to act, the eyebrows and beard fall; but if one does not intend, what then? Thereupon—
He called out loudly to the attendants, picked up his staff, and descended from the seat.
On the ninth day there was no white wine; they ate their fill of yellow chestnut cakes. On the tenth day there were yellow chrysanthemums; they urge one to harvest the grain.

Before the watchman's bell has even sounded at the fifth watch, the neighbor’s rooster has already crowed several times. When meeting on the road, do not dismount your horse; each must hasten toward their own future.
Yesterday the weather was warm; today the sky is cold. Heaven and earth both exert their power, yet the patch-robed monks have wide-open eyes.
Those who enter through the gate do not possess the family treasure. But what, then, is the family treasure?
He raises his staff, calls to the assembly, and asks: "Do you see it? He then knocks on the incense altar, sighs repeatedly, and says: "The Old Śākyamuni cannot be struck with a staff."
Kill! Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra do not turn their heads when called. Enough, enough! To exert effort in vain—just go with the flow. Wait for the season to arrive;
when a single leaf falls, it is autumn throughout the world.
Under the gate of Dongshan, when one wishes to walk, one walks; when one wishes to sit, one sits.
To defecate in the alms bowl and spit into the water pitcher while practicing by clinging to the Dharma is like an ox pulling a millstone.
Under Dongshan’s gate, when one needs to speak, one speaks; when one needs to act, one acts. One may save the eyebrows, but lose the nostrils.
He then gave a shout and said: "Long rains have not cleared. *Chan*!"
Upon returning from leaving the monastery, [Dongshan] said: "Not seeing one another for three days, one must not look with the old eyes. What kind of words are these?
Dongshan, having not seen [his teacher] for several days, met him and realized it was simply the person of old; he then joined his palms and said, "I hope you have been well. [The Master replied:
"The Buddhas of the past, the Buddhas of the present, and the Buddhas of the future. After the session ended, they drank tea together.
Under the gate of Dongshan, at times he blends mud with water; at other times he stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.
You all intend to see Dongshan in the place where he blends mud with water, yet Dongshan is not to be found there.
You intend to see Dongshan in the place where he stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high, yet Dongshan is not to be found there either.
If you intend to go everywhere to see Dongshan, know that Dongshan does not reside anywhere at all;

do not seek to see Dongshan, for the nose-rope is already in Dongshan’s hand. If you intend to nod off to sleep, he will pull the nose-rope with a jerk, and you will find your eyes flickering open, yet still unable to recognize him. I do not require you to recognize Dongshan; rather, you must recognize yourself.
That is so. To cite:
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the house style of the Master? He replied, "When a scholar comes, report it.
"Virtuous ones," he said, "a thousand hearings are not equal to one seeing. But how does one see? It is precisely because it is too clear that it, on the contrary, causes one to..."
It is attained slowly.

When the light shines, shave your head; when it is clean, wash your bowl. If it is good, stay; if it is bad, leave. O virtuous practitioners of meditation, do not use worldly views to bury the mind of the Way.
The trousers have no crotch and the breeches have no opening; on his head are three or five pecks of green ash. This old fellow from Zhaozhou is showing off too much.

Yet, as the saying goes: "In the state of Guoqing, the talented are noble; when a family is wealthy, the children are arrogant. Alas, while the grain does not ripen under the sun’s heat, they compete to plant peach and plum trees in spring.
This causes those who toil at the plow to spend half their lives as flower sellers.
"Simply being free from delusion is called liberation, yet in reality, one has not attained all-encompassing liberation.
What is this 'all-encompassing liberation'? He suddenly picked up his staff and said, "The Barrier.
He then said, "Master Yunmen was leaping about on the tip of my staff; do you see Cuiyan’s eyebrows? If you do not see them, Dongshan shall explain them for you."
Changqing arrived. He then threw down [the whisk] and said: "The flute is blown and the drum is beaten; everyone is invited to look!

If you rely on intellectual understanding and mental arrangements, or labor at artificial constructions, you will remain constantly clinging to external conditions and neglect your own fundamental task.
You would not believe that the True All-Knowing One of our own house could fail to achieve perfect enlightenment even after kalpas. He gave a shout.
Fenzhou, do not harbor deluded thoughts! Juzhi’s finger—here, the matters of the Buddhadharma of all time and antiquity come to a simultaneous rest.
Rest, rest! Yet I recall Zhaozhou’s examination of the old woman; even where there is no elegance, there is elegance.
To let it pass is one move; to fall into it is the second. In the middle of spring, the weather gradually warms and the scenery is bright and beautiful.

All you eminent gentlemen, are your daily activities light and well? Is there anyone among you who is not touched by the conditions of spring? After a long silence, he said: "Traveling afar, holding an empty bowl."

Treading upon fallen blossoms in the deep mountains, the Holy Monk speaks for all of you every day, reaching into your very bones and marrow; now that the drum has been struck, he proclaims it once more.
To wait further for an elder to open his mouth and move his tongue—what would that even be fit for? When I, this old monk, speak thus, it is like drawing legs on a snake.
This matter is like a bright pearl upon a platter: it turns of itself without being pushed. Some push it and it does not turn; they press it and it does not come alive. Furthermore...
How can one blame this old monk? Do you wish to recognize the bright pearl? Each of you return to the hall to drink tea.
On the twentieth day of the twelfth month, the entire assembly at Xinfeng—the very core of the patch-robed monks—is like a drop of water turned to ice.
When people are poor, their wisdom is short; when a horse is thin, its hair is long. Zhaozhou said, "In Qingzhou, I made a cotton robe that weighed seven catties.
The Master said, "He has years but no virtue; he saw the hare and released the hawk—he knows life but does not know death.
Assembly, if you wish to transcend birth and death without falling into the extremes of existence or non-existence, so that the Great Function manifests before you, do not follow after words.

Within the Dharma-gate of the Buddha, there is both granting and taking away. As for granting: there are four or five hundred lanes of flowering willows and two or three thousand towers of pipes and strings.
As for taking away: above the heavens and below the heavens, I alone am honored. As for neither granting nor taking away—how is this? After a long silence, he said:
"Always holding the flute for returning home, I blow it deep into the night across the Muzitan bend."

The Master of the Avataṃsaka School arrived and said, "The Dharma-realm is the fundamental substance of all sentient beings. He held up his staff and said, "It is not that this is not the Dharma-realm;
rather, it is the wondrous substance of you all—spiritually luminous, vast and penetrating, expansive, empty, and still—from beginningless time.
Therefore, whether in this land or other realms, in heaven or hell, among the six classes of ordinary beings and the four types of sages, or between the animate and the inanimate,"
They are identical and without difference; they are neither destroyed nor confused. Through the luminous pearls of the Indra’s Net, they mutually interpenetrate and flow into one another.

Thus, it may be said that the realms of infinite lands are not separated from oneself by so much as a hair’s breadth; the ten periods of past and present, from beginning to end, do not depart from the tip of a staff.
If this is so, then what need is there to mention casting the great trichiliocosm beyond the four quarters, or containing it within?
Mount Sumeru within a mustard seed; now, ten billion suns and moons, ten billion Mount Sumers, and ten billion worlds are all contained within this very staff.
He then threw it down, saying: "It has been cast before you all. Do you see it? Can you believe it?
This inconceivable power of liberation, this playful mastery of spiritual powers—its wondrous function is manifest right here, not dependent on anything else."
Other arts are all but the constant attributes of my own mind. (A shout. I descend from the seat.
The Stone of Asceticism is enveloped in moss; the Peak of Thrown Pens is entangled by *pi-li* vines. At the Arhat Hall, three novices are ordained each year;
at Guizong Temple, after the formal session, one drinks tea.
"You have a staff; I give you a staff. You have no staff; I take your staff away from you.
O assembly, this is a transaction for cash; do not let others deceive you. Do you understand? Whether there is profit or loss, it does not depart from the marketplace. Aha-ha!
I am reminded of Zhaozhou’s examination of the old woman—where there was no elegance, there was elegance nonetheless.

On the Mid-Autumn Festival of the eighth month, the cool breeze whistles and rustles. The patch-robed monks come and go like clouds or cranes. Whether north of the mountain or south of the mountain, there is a path that leads through;
they carry a single staff slung across their shoulders. It may be so, yet it may be so—never follow the footsteps of that old Lu, whether you are awakened or unawakened! (A shout.)

On the first day of the tenth month, it was said: "Ordinary people are obstructed by form; those of the Two Vehicles are obstructed by emptiness; Bodhisattvas are unobstructed regarding both form and emptiness. Before one's eyes, the myriad phenomena are arrayed;
principle and phenomena are harmoniously integrated and sovereign. In the Sangha hall, warm fires have been added once more. High adepts from the ten directions gather together;
there is no need to further distinguish between self and other, for we are all one true Dharma-realm. (He lets out a shout.)
This morning, the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month: one must know there is a Dharma that transcends words and phrases. Primordial clarity and primordial wondrousness require no cultivation;
a company of ancient Buddhas has gone into the hall.
After winter, the first yang arises; Qian and Kun dissolve and transform. Monks, do not sit and wait for the woodpecker to strike the stump.

Both are men of integrity; their daily life is the living reality of the true source. Everyone can see it for themselves—why then do you all ignore it? You merely follow along, turned by external things.

Within the gate of the patch-robed monks (*śramaṇa*), there is nothing that is not a realm of transcendent measure (*atimātra*). [The Master] enters into sovereign meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) and then shouts:
"Is this not a realm of transcendent measure? He then clears his throat and says: "Is this not sovereign meditative concentration? A-he-he!
To offer this profound mind to the dust-motes and lands—this is what is called repaying the Buddha’s kindness.
The great assembly must cease; there is no end in sight. Come together beneath the forest trees to study non-action (*wuwei*).
Wearing the *kāṣāya* upon our shoulders as fellow disciples of the Buddha—how much longer can we remain together when we meet?
"Great assembly, the ancients said: 'The entire earth is this gate of liberation. Yet people mistakenly take it as an object of Buddhist doctrine.
Why do they not see mountains as mountains and waters as waters? Guizong, however, says otherwise: 'The entire earth is this Dharma-gate of liberation.
Do not interpret it through the lens of intellectual views. Sometimes when seeing a mountain, do not call it a mountain; sometimes when seeing..."
"Water. Do not call it water. Great assembly, you men of integrity, do not allow yourselves to be deceived.
Great assembly, as for these two characters 'Buddha' and 'Dharma,' neither of them provides you with any advantage. Is there no lion cub among you?
I do not dare hope that you will let out a single roar to cause the eyes on the crowns of all heads in this assembly to open at once. For now, do not chew [on words]."
"The leftover soup and spoiled rice of the ancients—this too is acceptable. Today, Guizong deceives you all!
He took up his staff, threw it down, and said: "The turtle-nosed snake of Nanshan; those who know how to handle it, take it up! He let out a shout.
"Today at the Mountain Gate, we make offerings to the Arhats for the sake of the donors of the ten directions, to fulfill their heart's vows:

that the deceased may be reborn in heaven and those still living may obtain blessings. He called out, "Simply follow the custom and eat your rice; do not concern yourselves with the short or long duration of life in this world.
Again, lifting up his staff, he said: "My birth has been exhausted, the holy life is established, what was to be done has been accomplished."
Having received further existence, the three realms cannot do anything to him; he is worthy of receiving offerings from devas and humans.
This group of young forest-dwellers all deserve twenty blows of the staff. (He lets out a shout.)
"Great assembly, although we differ and our faculties and objects vary, their nature is inherently equal. There is no one who is 'equal';
if even equality does not exist, how much less can there be inequality? (Holding up the staff) Sentient and insentient beings share a single body;
everywhere is the same true Dharma-realm. (Then he throws it down) "It falls, yet it is not another thing. Now tell me: what is it?
"What thing? [He] lets out a shout.
"Days pass and months come; long and short months alternate. As time has already slipped away, birth and death draw near.
O assembly, you are all guests under the gate of the Patriarchs; you must know that birth and death are not mutually related. Now tell me, why does Guizong speak in this way?
"Is there anything more? After a long silence, he said: 'My parents did not permit me; I could not leave the household life. The Great Teacher, the Tathāgata, said:
'If one cannot realize one's own mind, how can one know the Right Path? Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Hanshan said:
'In a single thought, realizing one's own mind, one opens the Buddha’s knowledge and vision. Assembly, what is this? Realize it directly and take hold of it."
Holding up his staff, he said: "Who does not see this? Who does not know this? Knowing and seeing are distinct and clear. He then struck the meditation seat and said:
"Who does not hear this? Who does not understand this? Understanding is the equality of mind. To observe in this way is called right observation;
to observe otherwise is called wrong observation. With a thump, he set the staff down.
The Boatman went down to Yangzhou; throughout the great earth there is not an inch of soil. The sound of a snake biting a toad—there is further suffering for sentient beings.
He picks up his staff, hurls it down, and says: "Today is the twenty-fifth. He lets out a shout.
When a single leaf falls, autumn comes to the world. From the north of Mount Lu to Jiangzhou, he threw down his staff and said:
"If you know that what has fallen is not another thing, you must believe that in every direction you attain freedom."
This morning is the first day of the ninth month; the night brought with it a cold, frosty air. You should know that every path outside this gate leads straight through to Chang’an.
(A shout. This day has already passed, and life likewise diminishes accordingly. Like a fish in scant water, what joy can there be? Only the meditation of the Two Vehicles [remains].
Concentration is the bliss of quiescence; this is true bliss. For a Bodhisattva training in Prajñā, the bliss of Dharma-joy and the rapture of dhyāna is true bliss.
The compassion, joy, equanimity, and loving-kindness—the four immeasurable minds—of the Buddhas of the three periods of time constitute bliss;
this is true bliss. Shishuang Puhui said: "Rest! Cease! Go into a state of cold stillness! This is called the vehicle of the two vehicles.
The bliss of tranquil extinction. Yunmen said, "All-encompassing wisdom penetrates without obstruction. He raised his fan and said, "Śākyamuni Buddha has arrived!
This is called the bliss of Dharma-joy and Chan-delight. Deshan’s staff and Linji’s shout are the bliss of the compassion, joy, and equanimity of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Apart from these three kinds of bliss, there is nothing that constitutes bliss. Furthermore—

after the session ends, there will be tea."

In the ten directions, we gather as one; each and every one studies non-action (*wuwei*). This is the field for selecting a Buddha; with an empty mind, one returns having passed the imperial examination.

Great assembly, you are all people who have come to select a Buddha. Having arrived under the gate of Guizong, each and every one of you must return with an empty mind and having passed the examination.
You must not become merely long-term monks of the rice porridge and gruel. Both of us have left the secular world to become renunciants—who [else could do this]?
It is said that the Patriarch alone possessed the Southern Can (Nan-neng).

"Today is the fifteenth of the third month; once again the moon is full, facing the door. Whether the intent of the Patriarchs and the intent of the Teachings are the same or different, let us see the rooster climb the tree when cold.

The second day of the month: wherever the eyes turn and whatever conditions are encountered, the Dharma-gate is grandly opened. "It is better to go back. After a long silence, he said: "Where do you go?

He sells it at the head of the river. Even so, if one were to have Zhuo Wenjun (Muzi) look into a bright mirror, she would say, "There is no need to apply rouge.
Upon arriving at Qixian, he said: "Since Chengtian first opened the hall, I have been arranging some entanglements here in Shan-nan, to the east."
Kakushin Kaku: "However, while at Kuei-tsung and K'ai-shan, I have already settled all matters once and for all.

Today, arriving here at the assembly of San-hsia, it is much like trying to treat a goiter on the eve of a wedding; my hands and feet are at a loss for what to do. I hope the great assembly will not take offense.
I humbly pray that you all will cherish yourselves."
On the New Year’s Day, it is said: "Today, throughout the world beneath heaven, everyone has added one year to their age.
Now tell me: does the water buffalo also add one? Let us set aside for a moment whether he adds or not; rather, tell me, how much do the water buffalo's nostrils weigh?
If you can know the weight of his nostrils with perfect clarity, then let him ravage the crops of others as he pleases. If you have not yet reached this point, [it is like] the month of December."
The thirtieth day. Do not say that when spring comes, the grass grows green of its own accord.
Within heaven and earth, amidst the universe, there is a treasure hidden within the mountain of form.
O assembly, the eyes are above the nose, and the feet are below the belly. But tell me, where is this treasure? Then he said: "I do not know where the human face is."
"Go! The peach blossoms still smile at the spring breeze.
When Mañjuśrī gave rise to views of Buddhahood and views of the Dharma, he was banished by the World-Honored One to Mount Cakravāḍa.

"O Great Assembly, during the World-Honored One’s single period [of teaching], this was like losing a small dispute; it was a great loss of the marks of a Great Man. Now, if there were someone who, upon hearing..."
"Your Majesty, here! If you give rise to views of a Buddha or views of the Dharma, we, Your Majesty, will never dare to disturb them. Why is this so?
Simply by allowing the snow to melt away, spring will naturally arrive."

The superior person hears the Way and practices it with diligence; the mediocre person hears the Way and is as if it exists and yet as if it is lost; the inferior person hears the Way and laughs at it.
O Assembly, if we speak from the standpoint of the Zen monk’s school, we actually grant that the one who laughs possesses some backbone.
Why is this so? Because the eyes of the great assembly cannot be deceived.
He held up his staff and said, "Leaping upon the edge of a sword. Then, holding the staff horizontally across his chest, he said, "Riding a horse through a speck of dust;
toiling away, going and coming again—this is the one who knows. He threw down the staff and descended from the seat.
He gathers the profound mechanism before its signs appear; he conceals the dark operation within the very process of transformation. Great assembly, consider the Chan practitioners of today:
one by one they emerge with a bearing like that of kings; when questioned, their eloquence flows like a cascading river—what can be done about them?
Yet, if they could suddenly bring down the clouds from their heads and listen to what Tian says, these words of "having something as if there were nothing"—only then would they often come to know.
Beating the drum and playing the lute on the Way, we meet as two members of the same household. Although it is thus, where the power of Yu did not reach, the sound of the river flows toward the west.
This morning marks the beginning of the season; on this day, the first yang arises. Holding up his staff, he said: "Tell me, what is this?
If you can grasp it just as it is, then you will accordingly receive the blessings of the moment. If you wait until the New Year’s Day to count it, it will be too late."
"There is still much snow ahead. Therefore, Chengtian said: "Out of ten utterances, nine are abandoned.
Why is this so? One should not plant thorns at the gate; otherwise, descendants in later generations will have their clothes snagged by them.
Even so, thirty years hence, Grandfather Lü will cast his line.
If it were always like today, then Chengtian would be deceiving you, the Venerable Elders;
if it were not like today, then Chengtian could not deceive you, the Venerable Elders. Why is this so? Because one sides with principle, not with kin.
Entering the forest without disturbing the grass; entering the water without disturbing the waves; entering among birds without disrupting their flight.

This, the Great Assembly, is the skill of letting go of the mooring rope once the boat has been launched. But tell me, how should a patch-robed monk act? [He] strikes the meditation seat once with his hand and says:
"Turning over mountains and seas to seek a true friend; stirring up heaven and earth to see the peace of an era."
He struck the meditation staff and said, "When a single bubble arises, the waves begin. He struck again and said, "When a single bubble arises, Mañjuśrī appears.

He struck three more times and asked, "What about this one? After a long silence, he said, "Who would have thought that amidst the distant mist and surging waves, there is yet another way of contemplating?"
The Buddha-body is unconditioned and does not fall into any numerical categories. But tell me:

from where do the six sense bases, the twelve links of dependent origination, the eighteen elements, and even the eighty-four thousand Dharma gates come? Striking the meditation seat with his hand, he said:
"A fine woman does not wear her wedding clothes."
The Master raised an instance where a monk asked Touzi, "How is it when one enters nirvana without severing afflictions?
Touzi made a grimace and said, "This monk is well-suited for creating karma that kills. Xitang spoke otherwise, saying, "Every household has an Avalokiteśvara.
"Great assembly," [the Master continued], "Touzi may be called one who is skilled at assessing talent; Xitang may be called one who is skilled at filling a vacancy. Now, suppose suddenly—"
Someone asked Yuan Tong, "How is it when one enters nirvana without severing afflictions? He replied to him:
"Green mountains and blue waters; a short oar and a solitary boat."
A monk asked, "Before Niu-tou had seen the Fourth Patriarch, why did the hundred birds offer him flowers? The Master said, "Worldly sentiments perceive cold and warmth;
human faces follow high and low. "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "In the boiling cauldron, there is no place that is cool.
"What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "The crow flies and the hare runs. He then said, "If you establish even a single speck of dust, the state and the family..."
When there is prosperity, the village elder frowns; when not a single speck of dust remains [in order], the state and its family perish, yet the village elder remains at ease.
The assembly, tell me: is this it? Or is it not? After a long silence, he said: "The heart does not betray others; the face shows no shame."
He struck the meditation seat once with his hand and said, "Study!
Life and death alternate; cold and heat shift in turn. That things flow and change is the common condition of humanity.
Master Zhaoruan, however, stubbornly did not know that there is something which does not flow as a thing. What is this which does not flow? Liang.
Jiuyun said: "In a large month there are thirty days; in a small month there are twenty-nine.

Leaves fall and return to the root. When one comes, there are no lips. "Great assembly," he continued, "the Patriarch may truly be said to have been skilled at borrowing another's hand to perform his own fist."
There are certain people who often say, "The words are still ringing in my ears. But have they not heard it said: "When Ziqi departed and did not return, how deeply lamentable was that vast expanse!
One knows not who else among heaven and earth can truly be a connoisseur of music."
A bird has two wings; in its flight, there is no distance near or far. The Way emerges from a single corner; in its progression, there is no before or after.

You patch-robed monks, in your daily lives, set down your spoons and pick up your chopsticks, all claiming you "know it exists. Yet when you reach the top of the mountain pass, why do you suddenly become so short of breath?
It is not that the Way is unseen; it is simply that if a person lacks far-reaching foresight, they will inevitably face immediate distress.
When the river moon shines upon the pines and the wind blows, is there anyone here who has not passed through the net? After a long silence, he said:
"The August Heaven shows no partiality."
The Elder Śākyamuni has four great vows: "I vow to sever the boundless afflictions; I vow to study the boundless Dharma-gates;
I vow to deliver the boundless sentient beings; I vow to realize unexcelled Bodhi. The Lotus Sūtra also possesses these four great vows:
when hungry, one must eat; when cold, one must add clothing; and when weary, one stretches out one's legs and sleeps.
In a hot place, one desires the wind to blow.
This was the evening *xiaochan* (small private instruction) following the initial dwelling on the *Lotus Sūtra*. During the interval, [the Master] raised the case of Yangqi asking Ciming:

"The dark birds warble their songs; leaving the clouds, they enter the tangled peaks. What is it like at such a time? Ciming said: "I walk amidst the wild weeds; you, moreover, have entered a deep village."
Qiyun said, "The official does not permit even a needle. He asked another question. Ming then shouted. Qiyun said, "A fine shout!
Ming shouted again. Qiyun also shouted. Ming shouted twice in succession. Qiyun then bowed and withdrew.
The Master said, "Great assembly, you must know that one who has attained awakening when meeting others on the crossroads of the street, is nonetheless captured atop a thousand peaks."
Shaking hands. Meeting atop a thousand peaks, yet shaking hands at a crossroads. I, this mountain monk, have once offered a verse:
"Where others dwell, I do not dwell; where others walk, I do not walk. It is not that I find it difficult to dwell with others;
it is simply that the distinction between the monastic and the lay must be clear."

Ascending the hall for the opening of the session, after the question-and-answer exchange has concluded, he says: "In days of yore at the assembly on Vulture Peak, the World-Honored One held up a flower, and Kāśyapa smiled.
The World-Honored One said, 'I possess the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye; I entrust it to Mahākāśyapa so that it may be transmitted and never allowed to be severed.
As for this very day, if it were that Treasury of the True Dharma Eye, the Old Śākyamuni himself—"
There is no division. With what would one entrust it? With what would one transmit it? Within the sphere of each person, there is individually the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye.
From the moment they rise each day, they engage in judgments of right and wrong, distinguishing between south and north, and perform all manner of activities.
All of this is but the radiance and reflection of the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye.
When this eye opens, the heavens and earth, the sun, moon, and stars, and the myriad phenomena of the universe are all present before one’s eyes, yet not even a hair’s breadth of form is perceived.

When this eye has not yet opened, all these things reside within the very eyes of everyone. This does not apply to those who have already opened theirs; as for those who have not yet opened theirs, I, the mountain monk, [shall act as their guide].
For the sake of all people, he opens this treasury of the Dharma-eye. Look! He then raises two fingers and says, "Look, look!
If you can see it, matters will be as one family. If not, I cannot help but repeat these verses: 'The Dharma-eye treasury of all people—none of the thousand sages can equal it.
For your sake, I have opened a single thread; its radiance fills the Great Tang. Mount Sumeru enters the sea... Six.

The moon descends with bitter frost. Thus spoke the *Lotus Sūtra*; there is no phrase by which to deliberate. Since he has spoken it fully from his mouth, why is there no phrase by which to deliberate?
He lets out a shout and says: "Divide yourself into two places and look!"
"Just as when I press my finger, the Sea-Seal (Sāgaramudrā) emits light," [the Master] took up his staff and said:
"Mountains, rivers, the great earth, waterfowl, and forest trees—sentient and insentient alike—all issue forth a great lion’s roar from the tip of this staff, expounding the Mahāprajñāpāramitā.
Now tell me, what Dharma-gate do Tiantai and Nanyue preach? Nanyue preaches the Five Ranks of Dongshan."
Cultivating practice: Ruler and subject, father and son, each attains their proper place. Do not cling to the remote crags where strange grasses grow green;

sitting amidst the white clouds, the lineage is not yet perfected. Tiantai speaks of Linji’s Three Mysteries and Three Essentials, the Four Kinds of Discernment, and how a single shout distinguishes guest from host.
When illumination and function proceed simultaneously, if you wish to understand the meaning therein, it is like striking the third watch at midday. Thus spoke Lushan.
"Dao! You two fellows are right in the midst of a tangle of vines. Have you not heard it said:
'If you wish not to incur the karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the Tathāgata’s True Wheel of Dharma'?

As for the insights of these three fellows, if they were weighed on the scale of a true monk, one would weigh eight *liang*, another half a *jin*, and the other would not be worth even half a coin. Now, and so forth...
The Way. That fellow is not worth half a penny. I only wish that the spring breeze would exert its full strength and blow all at once into my gate.
Once, when Jinkan was in front of the kitchen, he saw the head cook and asked, "Head cook, how do you transform the raw into the cooked?"
"It is not that there is no kitchen steward. Put aside the wooden ladle and bring me a phrase. The steward was speechless.

Later, he had a monk enter the room to provide a substitute response, but none were in accord with the truth. He then provided his own substitute, saying: "Though the mutton soup is delicious, many mouths are difficult to satisfy. The assembly, tell me:
has the Golden Phoenix (Jinluan) been able to part from the wooden ladle yet? Fahua, however, is not like this; having parted from the wooden ladle—[one phrase].
A phrase. How would you say it? When human relations are harmonious, even drinking water makes one fat.
This year the rain has been exceptionally abundant; take it for granted that the world will have a bountiful harvest this autumn.
Cowherds everywhere sing songs of peace, making old Wang the Elder from the eastern village laugh to death.
He was invited by Hefei, but did not go. Returning to the mountain, he said: "I do not dwell in the city god’s precincts; indeed, it was as I had expected.
Mountain flowers and mountain birds again share in my joy. Last night, the stone spring passed before my window; why is its clear sound superior to it was of old?
He struck his staff three times.
Xuan Sha once accidentally took some medicine, and his entire body became red and festering. A monk asked, "What is the solid, enduring Dharma-body?
Xuan Sha replied, "Dripping pus. Master Tiantai Huai wrote a verse on this: "Drip by drip, his whole body is festering pus;
Upon the fishing boat, he displays the family style. People of the time see only the fishing line, But fail to see the red smartweed facing the reeds."
There was once a person who asked about the *Lotus Sūtra*: "What is the pure Dharma-body? He simply answered him, saying, "The stench of excrement permeates the heavens.
He further said, "A child is born by transformation upon a lotus petal. Now tell me: is he the same as the ancients, or is he different?
The Lotus Sutra also contains verses: "The stench of excrement perfumes the heavens; this too is merely coincidental. How would the Lotus Sutra dare proclaim it for you?
If there were a passage through the nose reaching heaven, one might roam at will without being pierced."

Quoting Xuedou, he said: "The spring mountains layer upon layer of chaotic green; the spring waters ripple with empty azure. Vast and silent between heaven and earth, standing alone, what limit can one’s gaze reach?
He then turned back to his attendant and asked, "Is there anyone guarding the abbot’s quarters?

The attendant replied, "There is. Xuedou himself then said, "The heart of a thief is always apprehensive. This old man Xuedou, letting go and gathering in, possesses the power to expand and contract the very cosmos.
[The Master] raised his hand. Although it is thus, how can it be that heaven and earth cannot contain it? Yao and Shun did not know its name; the Lotus [Sūtra] could not restrain its brilliance.
On behalf of the ancients, I shall give vent to my spirit: Mountain cherries glow like flames; mountain birds sing in swarms with liquid clarity.
Hand in hand, we do not share the same path; let the spring air blossom as it will. Since heaven and earth first came into being, how many have possessed living eyes? The Dharma.
As soon as the flower briefly appeared, he did not even pause to question his attendant, but immediately descended from the seat.

Regarding the Summer Retreat (Jie Xia), it is said: "The beginning of the *an-guo* (sitting in peace) is named 'prohibiting the feet' (*jin zu*). The meaning of 'prohibiting the feet' lies in the intent to advance on the Path and protect living beings.
But for us practitioners of the patched robe (*na seng*), what living being is there to protect, and what Path is there to advance upon? Spit! Spit! Spit it all to pieces!"
When the Old Man Śākyamuni takes a single step, he tramples through the spinal column of Śākyamuni himself;
yet this is still merely following in the footsteps of the crowd. This is not yet a monk of the fundamental division. What, then, is a monk of the fundamental division?
With boundless elegance, he is too weary to put it on display, thereby sparing others from pointing at him as a "fine gentleman."
Even if one were to pour out ten thousand taels of gold every day, it would not suffice for the gateway of the *Lotus Sūtra*.

Even if one were worth no more than half a penny, one might just manage to enter the gateway of the *Lotus Sūtra*, yet one has not yet ascended to the hall of the *Lotus Sūtra*, nor entered the chamber of the *Lotus Sūtra*.
Tell me, what kind of person can ascend to the hall of the *Lotus Sūtra* and enter its chamber? [His] eyes are triangular; his head is as sharp as the Five Peaks.
The *Lotus Sūtra* has gathered three kinds of rare treasures that have seldom been brought forth in ordinary times.

Today, as the hemp heads and grain heads set out, I cannot help but produce them and present them to you all. (He raises his staff and strikes it three times. He says: "First of all, do not split this open;
furthermore, it must be divided equally between the two. Even if one encounters a foreign merchant captain from the South, [it remains so]."
"You must exchange your very eyes.
To realize the Way upon hearing sound, and to clarify the mind upon seeing form. [He spreads his two hands and asks: "Is there? Is there? [Then he shakes his hand.]
"No, no. It is said: 'Having once crossed the great ocean, one need not boast of its waves; were it not for Mount Wu, all else would be but mist.
He struck the meditation seat once.
"This matter is like being at the edge of a ten-thousand-fathom cliff. Everyone knows this; let go! Then you will plunge to the bottom.
It is simply that one cannot bring oneself to give up one's life. On this day, Fahua, without moving a single hair’s breadth, instructs everyone to go to the very bottom.
He then threw down his staff and descended from the seat.
In studying the Way, one must first learn poverty. Once you have learned poverty, the Way will become intimate.

When one day you realize the Way of being poor, the functioning of the Way will be like that of a poor person. Although I, Fahua, travel the same road as the ancients, I do not return by the same road as the ancients.
Why is this so? I dwell in my own small courtyard; when guests arrive, I have nothing to bestow upon them.
Even if there were nothing left to chew upon, one relies on those below to provide support, so that day by day things can still be covered over.
It may be said: "The mountain flowers do not neglect the power of cultivation; the spring breeze naturally takes care of them."
The donor offered his Dharma robe and said, "A dragon wears even a single thread; the garuḍa will not swallow it.
Had he swallowed it all in one gulp at that time, would the world not have been at peace? But tell me, which is that which cannot be swallowed?
He picked up a corner of the robe and showed it to the assembly, saying, "Is this not that which cannot be swallowed? Do you see it? It hangs there quite casually."
On his shoulders, he was superior to those people of the age wearing brocade robes.
Residing at Longmen, a monk asked, "What is the realm of Longmen? The Master said, "Only upon arriving will you know. "What is the person within the realm?
The Master said, "Both feet planted firmly on the ground. He then said, "If seeing and hearing are not shed, it is like the moon in the water."
Mountain colors and the sound of water; famous flowers and extraordinary birds fill the eyes and ears.
How can one speak of the principle of liberation? Do you wish to understand? It is vast! It is vast! Old Śākyamuni has no skill at all. Enough! Enough!
The mountains and waters of Longmen are the most secluded in the world. Last night I slept until dawn; where there is elegance, let there be elegance.

All sounds are the Buddha’s voice; all forms are the Buddha’s form. Śākyamuni the Old Man has deceived the men and women of households, causing them to fall into the Avīci Great Hell, where they remain to this day without being able to emerge.
[The Master] raises his staff and says: "The butcher Xiang Daobei from Lake Tai County has today, upon the tip of the Dragon Gate staff, attained [enlightenment]."
"Attaining Equal and Perfect Enlightenment, turning the Great Dharma Wheel, and delivering all sentient beings—do you people see this?
If you do see it, there will be peace throughout the world. (He strikes the meditation seat with his staff.)
A monk cited a question asked of Zhaozhou: "The Third Patriarch, the Tripitaka Master with the Large Ears, searched for the National Teacher three times and could not find him.
Zhaozhou said, 'He is inside the Tripitaka Master’s nostrils. A monk asked Xuansha, 'Since he is inside the nostrils, why can he not see him? Xuansha said, 'It is precisely because he is too close.
[The Master continued,] 'Everyone, if the National Teacher were inside the Tripitaka Master’s nostrils, what difficulty would there be? "

[The Master] said, "I see. Yet you do not realize that while you are engaged in such contemplation within the eyes of the Tripitaka, the Buddhas of the ten directions all appear before you. Now tell me, how do you contemplate?
If you contemplate with a mind of attachment, the entire earth becomes a forest of thorns; if you contemplate with a mind of non-attachment, the entire earth becomes a wasteland."
Cen remained silent for a long while, then said: "Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the valley.
In studying Chan and the Way, do not be in such a hurry. To penetrate the Dharma-body is like finding the Big Dipper hidden away.
Now that I am old and worn out, I am too indolent to deliberate with others. Only my hoe knows my way, as I walk together upon the pine-covered peaks."
Vajra. The old master Dongshan Cong may truly be said to have gathered his profound mechanisms before they manifested and concealed his dark workings within the very process of transformation;
his style is difficult for anyone, past or present, to equal. As for me, an old man at Longmen, I am daily struck down by a stifling qi in my chest;
day by day it grows worse. I see only emaciation and am truly without strength to discuss matters with others. Nevertheless, although it is thus—
It is so. A family may be poor, yet wish for their neighbor to be wealthy.
Sometimes the pestle-head blossoms with flowers; sometimes the Buddha’s face displays a hundred uglinesses.
When Master Li falls drunk on the street, it is simply because Master Zhang is drinking wine. The lantern wrinkles its brow in distress; the pillar laughs aloud and claps its hands.

For those who have not yet penetrated through, first teach them to recognize; for those who have already penetrated through, you must walk together with them. The entire earth is the single eye of a śramaṇa.
To whom can one teach to recognize the ground of ultimate reality? Where can one walk when not receiving even a single speck of dust?
Therefore it is said: "Where worldly people dwell, I do not dwell; where others travel, I do not travel. It is not that I find it difficult to dwell together with others;
rather, it is that the distinction between the monastic and the lay must be clear. Subtract a little from where there is little; add a little to where there is much. Why?
Because one subtracts even more from what is already little, and adds even more to what is already much. This is a secret of the immortals, not transmitted even between father and son.
Today he speaks of this; tomorrow he speaks of that. What is "that"? A lacquer bucket—go to the hall for practice.
Even the Dharma should be relinquished, how much more so that which is not the Dharma. Holding up his staff, he said: "As for this staff, what do you make of it?"
"Let go. Again, he asked, "How would you explain what is not the Dharma? After a long silence, he said, "Knock off the nostrils; let the eyes be exposed.
He struck the meditation seat.
If you do not understand a single dharma, it will cloud your eyes. [The Master] lifts up his staff and says, "Is this not the eye?
Within the eighty-four thousand dharma-gates, there is not a single shadow. Within the eighty-four thousand dharma-gates, every gate is liberation.
How could anything cloud it? It is just like seeing mountains and seeing waters every day, and discriminating between blue, yellow, red, and white."

[The Master] said, "It is not it. Furthermore, how do you see? He then struck his staff once and said, "Blind! A monk sat cross-legged in the sutra hall. One day, the Librarian asked him, "Why do you not read the sutras, Elder?
The monk replied, "I do not know how to read characters. The Librarian said, "Why do you not ask someone else? The monk bowed with palms joined and said, "I do not yet understand..."
"What character is this? The Master remained silent. "Great assembly, although the Librarian is silent, how can one deny that his voice is like thunder?
Although this monk does not recognize the character, its strokes and dots are nonetheless distinct. Tell me, what character is it?
After a long pause, he said: "Look for it within the *Yupian*."
When a thief comes, you must strike; when a guest comes, you must look upon them. When a guest comes, you must look upon them; this is the constant way of propriety.
But tell me: how do you strike when a thief comes? A human face resembles that of a thief, and a thief’s face resembles that of a human.
At the third watch of the night, what means is there for discernment? Nevertheless, even so, one must not let him pass. (With this, he struck once with his staff.)
As for the two characters "Buddha-Dharma," it would not be out of place for them to vanish to another world-system;
however, once or twice a day, the alms bowl must remain moist—not a single drop less. It is not as the saying goes: "Hearing of one full meal makes one forget a hundred hungers.
Today, this mountain monk’s own body is the very proof of that. Thus he said: "How do you do? How do you do?"

I have told you this before: it is not yet so. There is no other meaning; it is simply that for all of you to eat porridge or rice, you must personally take up the spoon and hold the chopsticks to be truly full. If you rely on someone else to provide them for you, it is merely a hollow satiety.
On the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, one merely wins a mouthful of dry saliva. Even so, do not let it be forgotten that the Ocean Assembly has opened its hall.
After the question-and-answer session concludes, he says: "One who is skilled in speaking speaks what cannot be spoken;
one who is skilled in tracing traces traces what cannot be traced. Every day, opening the mouth and moving the tongue is nothing other than speaking. What is this?
To speak of that which cannot be spoken by words—once it is called "words," it is already a trace.
How can one speak of that which cannot be traced? At this point, the entire great treasury of the teachings is of no use whatsoever. At this point...
Throughout the entire great treasury of the teachings, every single word is put to use. Why is this? Because at first it is not put to use, yet later it is indeed put to use.
Now tell me, where does the point of confusion lie? Have you not heard it said: "The momentum of a thousand peaks ceases upon reaching the mountain peak"?

The sounds of ten thousand streams vanish upon returning to the sea. From antiquity to the present day, those who have drilled into and gazed up toward this [truth] are as numerous as rice, hemp, bamboo, and reeds;

yet those who have truly and thoroughly penetrated it are not even one or two in a hundred. If you can indeed penetrate it, then throughout the twelve periods of the day, you will experience unimpeded joy and liberation.
Responding to circumstances and engaging with beings, you will bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings, as vast as the heavens, the stars, and the sun.
The Moon. The entire earth, with its grasses, trees, and forests, is all made into a single arena for coming and going and play.
An ancient said: "The turning of jade and the rolling of pearls—such words of the Buddhas and Patriarchs are still defilements to the mind-field.

Old Lu only knows how to husk rice; how could he have transmitted the legacy of Huangmei for ten thousand ages? When I, this mountain monk, am in my hermitage, I also have instructions for my disciples.
"Though there is indeed nothing at all directly beneath, it is still difficult to remain alive if one has not fully penetrated through it. Last night, a wild wind arose at the sea gate;
infinite waves were swept away in a single stroke. At such a moment, he first clears the path for others, and then takes both hands and places it before them.
Those who are quick-witted need not exert even a hair’s breadth of effort to grasp it and carry it away. Is there anyone?

If it does not go forth, I dare ask you all: throughout the twelve periods of the day, in the application of activity and conduct, in distinguishing the worthy from the foolish and in discerning right from wrong—what is this?

Guo Gongfu entered the mountain. Ascending the hall, he said: "Last night upon my pillow, I composed a verse on the mountain to thank Guo Gongfu, a great scholar and a twenty-year old friend from Mount Lu.
Today he has come from afar to visit the white clouds; I shall present it to the assembly so that you may clearly transmit it to all quarters hereafter.
