The Iron Kunlun boy takes a tumble; the Persian from the South Sea cannot finish his dance. At midnight, he loses his waist-sash;
Old Uncle Wang of the eastern village laughs himself down. (He strikes the meditation seat once and descends.)
The entire body is painted with brocade, yet there is but bare bone and strength. The old woman selling fans shields her eyes from the sun with her hand.
A man without hands—every punch is a true punch. A fellow without feet—every kick is a true kick. Aha-ha! Nine times nine is originally eighty-one.
Level as a mirror, precipitous as a cliff. To deliberate is to lose it; to move is to deviate from it. Not to deliberate and not to move, yet one is still bound by oneself.
There is another vital function that digs the earth to bury itself. [He lets out a shout] and says: "Yunmen personally saw Chen the Sandal-Maker."
I request that Shaolin re-establish its monastic lineage. Before the Multi-Child Stupa, the wind blows and the grass bows;
beneath the gate of King Yuyewa, the true command is once again enacted. Overturning the old patterns of the past, let even Buddhas and Patriarchs beg for their lives.
This is neither the "First Phrase" nor a mechanism beyond the norm. As soon as a single nail enters the wood, sparks fly throughout the entire world.
When the dragon roars, mist rises; when the tiger howls, wind is born. When the water is deep, the boat is high; when the mud is thick, the Buddha is great. For what reason?
Where the power of spring does not reach, even withered trees bloom. After a long silence, he said: "Having secured Annam, one still worries about the north of the Great Wall."
[The Master] cites Nanquan’s instruction to the assembly: “The Way is not outside of things; that which is outside of things is not the Way.
Zhaozhou stepped forward and asked, “What is the Way that is outside of things? Nanquan pulled his staff and struck him. Zhaozhou caught the staff and said, “Do not strike me;
you may strike others by mistake in the future. Nanquan said, “Dragons and snakes are easy to distinguish, but it is difficult to deceive a patch-robed monk. Thus it is said.
He returned to the abbot’s quarters. The Master said, "You have escaped the swift thunder, yet you have encountered a second bolt of lightning.

The one who had been ill said, "The very substance of empty space is the illness; the myriad phenomena of the forest and the mountains are the medicine. This is called 'medicine and illness treating each other.
Even if it were to reach the point where empty space vanishes and the myriad phenomena sink into stillness, this would still not be the moment for 'no medicine. After a long silence...
It is said: "Vaiśālī has been lost; no one understands how to look at the arrow.
When Penglai opens its invitation, before the flower is even picked up—who can rely on them to cast an eye upon it? After the breaking smile, the transmission has already gone astray.

From this point on, they have merely echoed the sound and inherited the void, resulting in the sight of hemp wrapped in paper. Were it not for a man of true substance, it would be difficult to give rise [to awakening]."
This is the wind of the Gate: holding fast and letting go; heaven revolves and earth turns. An iron boat fears not the fury of the ocean waves;
one knows that the fragrant bait intends for the dragon. Please accept this at once; do not trouble yourself with modesty.
To cite the Way of True Purity: Shishuang said, "Rest! Cease! This refers to the bliss of the extinction of the Two Vehicles.
Yunmen said, "All-encompassing wisdom penetrates without obstruction. He raised his fan and said, "The Old Man Śākyamuni has arrived!
This refers to the joy of the Dharma and the delight of meditation experienced by Bodhisattvas studying Prajñā. The staff of Deshan and the shout of Linji—these are called... [the Great Function].
The joy of the Buddhas of the three periods of time consists of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity. Apart from these three types, nothing else constitutes joy.
The Master said: "The Old Man Zhenjing could recognize the joy of others, but he could not find joy in his own joy.
Within this very place, King Bimbasāra took climbing the mountain of blades and the tree of swords as joy; he took drinking molten copper and swallowing hot iron as joy. Do not..."
"Is there anyone who shares this joy? He gives a shout and says: "If you are not one who plays in the tide, do not enter the surging waves.
He cites Longya’s words: "My elder brother Yunju attained the second phrase; I have attained the first phrase.
Xiyuan asked Yunmen, "When Longya spoke thus, did he support the truth or not? Yunmen said, "One must first pay homage to Yunju."
[The Master] said, "Yes. Xiyuan said, "The bystanders laugh. The Master said, "Seeing injustice on the road, one draws the sword to assist;
if a turtle is wounded like a tortoise, it must surely have an owner."
Commander Fan entered the mountains. If we discuss the matters of the Chan school, it is like a supreme general facing the battlefield:

his strategic maneuvers and tactics are fully prepared, and his every word and gesture brings forth a wind of spiritual power. Thus, when it comes to Linji’s "Vajra King Sword," who would dare to meet its edge?
The secret code of Mount Dongshan cannot be fathomed even by ghosts or spirits. Its subtlety lies in establishing merit and building a legacy, assisting the state and securing the realm.
Even so, is there not yet a matter that transcends this? [He] strikes the meditation seat and says: "Look back at the place where he shot the eagle."
The evening clouds level across a thousand miles.
A monk asked, "What is the word that cuts through iron? The Master said, "Frost fills the mouth.
On the fifteenth day of the second month, there is no concealment or protection; mountain flowers, half red and half white, vie to bloom, while a yellow oriole sings out once.
Two voices speak at once: if you take the eye, the ear will surely go deaf; if you take the ear, the eye will be blind.
Baozi is hidden; Yunmen is revealed. The oil jar is smashed; the rat is lost.

Citing the Way of Dharma Master Zhao: "Observing the directions, one knows that there is going; yet the goer does not arrive at those directions. The Master said: "Observing the directions, one knows that there is going;
yet the goer does not arrive at those directions. Wanli is the city of Fanghu, but the calamity arises within the inner palace walls."
Holding up his staff, he addressed the assembly, saying: "If you call it a staff, it will bind you to death; if you do not call it a staff, it will drive you to death.
He struck the ground once and said: "The sail has already been hoisted with the wind; yet you are unwilling to board the ship."
Speech is slander; silence is deception. It does not reside in neither speaking nor remaining silent, nor does it lie in looking downward or upward.
[The Master] picks up his staff and strikes once, saying: "Opening the gate of ambrosia, revealing the true mark. He strikes again, saying:
"For no reason, he piles up green cliffs upon level ground."

Holding the whisk during a winter night discourse: where the teachings of the Great and Small Tripitaka fail to provide an explanation or commentary, one must thoroughly tear one’s straw sandals to pieces.

Even the four, seven, two, and three patriarchs—who transmitted the lineage from one to another—did not reach the bottom; they would not even eat what was fed to a dog. How much less could they have divided branches or established lineages?
This brings disgrace upon the ancestral tradition, causing one to merely follow the crowd and join the throng, mutually obstructing one another’s progress.

If we speak of the fundamental matter of a monk, looking at it blinds the eyes; listening to it deafens the ears; raising it rots the tongue; and understanding it leads straight to a descent into hell.
Only when you can plant your feet directly beneath it and push it wide open is it right to give three thousand blows in the morning and eight hundred in the evening.

A hundred [steps]. Standing upright like a sheer cliff ten thousand fathoms high, the land is vast and the people sparse; one cannot help but yield to the exigencies of the times and open a single path through.
Therefore it is said: "When the myriad yin lines are stripped away, how has a single hair ever been moved? When the first yang line returns, the entire mechanism is already leaked.
At such a moment as this, what is it like? Wild waters freeze into fragments of silver; the cold plum...
Snowflakes burst forth like scattered jade.
For ninety days, one restrains the feet; this creates the causes for hell. For three months, one dwells in retreat; yet bearing a cangue and wearing shackles, one must kill in order to protect life.
Only when all have been killed does one truly dwell in peace. If you can realize the meaning within this, an iron boat will float upon the water. Exhausting one's own [effort]—
The mind laughs until it splits the mouths of others. Taking Great Perfect Enlightenment as my monastery, body and mind dwell in peace within the wisdom of equanimity.

Such good people refuse to act accordingly; they stubbornly lie within the filth. Upon reaching this state, even if one cuts off the tracks of both sages and ordinary folk and does not occupy the rank of Buddhas or patriarchs, one may roam with ease even in demon palaces or tiger dens. Within the domain of the patch-robed monk, this is the case.

There is no connection whatsoever. If one were a blind donkey whose trampling startles the world, they would take a single step forward from this very point of no connection and immediately see that on Vulture Peak, Kāśyapa’s smile was a mistaken reception;
and before the Peak of Shaoshi, Huike’s attainment of the marrow was not yet intimate. Ultimately, how would you express that one phrase of intimacy? After a long silence, he said: "Night."
The half-moon star appears at midday; the deluded person still waits for the cock to crow at dawn.
On the anniversary of his parents' memorial day, Fo-zhao requested that [the Master] ascend the seat. Wondrously awakening to the profound mechanism, the red thread at one's heels is revealed.

Amidst the vast activity of great function, the thousand-year-old entanglements are severed by a man of transcendent capacity with a single stroke—no longer traveling the same path as the thousands of sages.
Holding up a single phrase, sweep away the lairs of all demons. Amidst the thorny thickets, smelt gold and carve jade;

upon the golden throne, scatter earth and fling sand. Turning heaven and overturning earth, it stands towering and majestic; surpassing antiquity and soaring above the present, its wind is chillingly fierce.
The thousand peaks are cut off; ten thousand acres of emptiness and stillness. The infinite debt of gratitude is repaid all at once. At this very moment, tell me:
where have the two honored spirits gone? Do you understand? Within the inner palace, Maitreya is seen upon the dais;
throughout the entire world, the pure Dharma-body is fully revealed. At the end, he spoke a verse: "Unprovokedly, King Śuddhodana and..."
Māyā gave birth to a son and did not rise from her bed. This day is hard to forget; on that day there was resentment.
A burner of aloeswood incense, a bowl of tea.
An ancient verse.
Cui Chan ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he said, "Come forth and I shall strike you!
Come forth and I shall strike you! A monk came forward and asked, "What about Cui Chan? Cui then threw down the staff and returned to his quarters.
Thirteen years accustomed to embroidered silken garments; I pity my own red sleeves as I catch their fragrance. People say these were from the time of my marriage.
Wearing it, one feels shame; the embroidered double mandarin ducks emerge.

— Words of Master Yong of Muan. Upon ascending the seat while serving as the successor to Master Lan’an at Xichan Temple, after the questions and answers were concluded, he said: "Where the myriad functions do not reach, even the thousand sages knit their brows. It is precisely...
If one were to attempt to practice this, who would dare to even conceive of it? Even if a Patriarch were to appear in the world, he could not avoid playing with the false as if it were the real.

To point directly at the human mind is like looking toward plum trees to quench one's thirst. Thus we know that on the single path prior to sound, even the wise remain bewildered; to claim mastery beneath a word is, in fact, a lapse.

Even if one possesses hands capable of leaping across a rushing torrent or crossing a blade without being wounded by its edge— [The text continues: ...even such a person cannot avoid being struck by the sharp point.
The entire army is victorious; this is precisely the realm of the patch-robed monks. As for guarding camps and holding fortresses, what use are there for old, weak, and exhausted soldiers?
Is there anyone present now who possesses the spirit to charge toward the heavens? After a long silence, he said: "The golden arrowhead, well-honed, has seen a hundred battles;
the iron whip is full of strength, yet it laments having no enemy."
When the wheel of the teaching turns upon the high seat, even those who are adept remain deluded. When the thousand eyes open at once, how can one understand?
Have you not seen Master Muzhou address the assembly, saying: "If you have not yet attained an entry point, you must attain an entry point. Once you have attained it..."
"Enter the gate! Do not fail this old monk by speaking such words; how thick is your face? Muduan said, "I am not like that.
You all have not yet attained an entry point; you must attain an entry point."
Residing at Yangyu Hermitage, he ascended the seat and said: "For years I have not crossed the path of Yunmen; I have been going along with the waves and currents like this.
Now that I am old and once again foolish and simple, I shall return to act as the master of a village hermitage.

I will ride a blind donkey and beat a poisonous drum, laying down both civil and martial arts upon the field of a hundred battles. Let Linji stir up the dust and smoke, and let Weiyang and Yangshan alternate their roles."

The ranks are arrayed; the positions of the soldiers are set with spears and banners. The three types of halberds and crossbows are deployed. Without even a single cough, they are instantly exposed and defeated.
Although this is so, it is still merely the ordinary usage. But as for that phrase which does not fall into the temporal moment—how is it?
After a long silence, he said: "Chop fresh firewood and burn it with the leaves; at times gather wild vegetables and cook them together."

The Root Boils; Raising It Again. When the monks arrived at Crane Forest (Heilin) and knocked on the door, the Master asked, "Who is it? The monks replied, "We are monks. He said, "Do not say you are monks;

even if the Buddha himself came, he would not be admitted. The Master said, "All you Zen adepts, although Heilin was indeed able to hold fast to his boundaries, he simply did not know how to adapt to high or low ground.
I, this mountain monk, am not like that—at the gate of my abbot’s quarters, there are eight [openings]."

The characters have been opened up. When the monk comes and the Buddha comes, there is nothing at all to obstruct them. Why is this so? If one has no servants, even a small ones, one cannot be called a gentleman.
The Emperor celebrated the calligraphy of the plaque for Myōki-an. The Master pointed to the tablet and said: "The tiger’s head with its horns—few can handle it.
Do not spread the sparks of flint and lightning too thickly. The Restorer of the Throne displays his divine edge; Among the myriad phenomena, behold it revealed alone."
He ascended the seat. After the question-and-answer session was concluded, he said: "The waves at the sea gate drum toward the sky; who among you knows the家风 (family style) of Miaoxi?
Today, wind and clouds again provide the opportunity; clearly, the supreme teaching is fully upheld. Before the patterns have manifested, the message has already been revealed.
Shaking the earth and startling the heavens, there is no room for evasion. The Milky Way shines forth and the stars hang down—who would dare [to look away]?"

Lifting his head, he stares with a direct gaze. He then raises the case again: Wuzu addressed the assembly, saying, "If someone were to take the four great oceans as an inkstone and Mount Sumeru as a brush, and write the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West across the vast void—if they could do so, I would descend from my seat and bow to them as my teacher;
if they cannot write it, then the Buddha-dharma has no efficacy. The Master said, "O Zen practitioners, even if you were to act in such a way..."
Not yet a master of the Way. Break open the golden lock of the mysterious pass; behold the skill that reaches the heavens!
Holding up his staff, he draws a line and says: "Do you understand? Three parts enter the stone, eternally wondrous; it causes the immortals to tremble in secret."
A letter from the Venerable Gumuk of Geumsan arrived, saying: "A withered tree blooms with flowers—a springtime beyond kalpas;
Its fragrance pervades the realm, heard by all throughout antiquity and today. Suddenly the tree falls—where does it return? Monkeys cry out across a thousand mountains as the moon fills the boat."
On the occasion of celebrating the Imperial Birthday, he ascended the seat and said: "Renowned as the foremost in both the mundane and supramundane realms, who dares to gaze directly at its head?
Today, in this joyful assembly of wind and clouds, the Dragon’s Countenance appears from the depths of the Nine Palaces. He raised his whisk and said:

How truly magnificent! How extraordinary! How truly magnificent! Such is his wealth and nobility; yet he has not departed from Tuṣita to descend into the royal palace. Between heaven and earth, there is none to equal him.
Ten thousand nations come to court, gazing up in reverence at his sage brilliance. The Southern Mountain once more displays its lush greenery.
It reaches such a point that dragons roar at the vermilion gates and phoenixes dance in the azure heavens; the stone shoots sprout new branches, and the wooden man...
Clapping his hands: "At this very moment, is there anyone who shares in the joy of ascending the bottomless [ground]? After a long silence, he said:
"The hawk-bow hangs high; the smoke of war has ceased. The mountains and rivers of the four hundred prefectures have been reclaimed."
Upon arriving at Xuefeng, he requested to ascend the seat and said: "Understanding speech does not depend on the tongue; the ability to speak does not reside in sound.
When neither sound nor tongue is employed, one returns home and puts an end to questioning the journey. Since it neither depends on the tongue nor resides in sound, how then does one speak?"

How can one listen? Since there is no speaking to be spoken, there is likewise no listening to be heard. One reaches the point where falling flowers find no path and both the mundane and the sagely leave no trace.
It is like a bright mirror set upon its stand: the frantic head (Evil Mañjuśrī) has ceased its pursuit of the paths east and west. The vast capacity for awakening rests within the palm of the hand.
Pushing back the Great Spirit (Guliang) and splitting the peaks of Mount Taihua—such divine majesty as this, who would dare approach?

Here, all the old monks of the world must suppress their breath and swallow their voices; they have no choice but to beg for their lives. Now, as the thread of the path is opened, I wish for everyone to know it exists.
[He raises his whisk and says: "To err by a hair’s breadth is to lose by a thousand miles. This is the true Linji.

The Dharma-eye treasury was extinguished before this blind donkey. To this day, the three hundred and sixty bones and joints, the eighty-four thousand pores—everything has been cast at once into the laps of all of you. I wonder, do you discern it clearly? (He strikes the whisk.
A single flash of stone-fire flies beyond the heavens; let people cease looking at the stars beside the moon. He spoke again: "Just now..."
Coming before the Elder of the Abbot’s Quarter, he cited a monk’s question to Wuzu Heshang: “What is the matter of Linji’s lineage?
Wuzu replied, “The five rebellions hearing thunder. The Master said, “Wuzu Heshang opens up a world within the eye of a gnat.”

Severing Linji’s tongue in a single sitting—do you know where it lands? Splitting open the vast ocean to seize and swallow the dragon, one is forbidden from hearing the thunder of the five heinous crimes.
Turning instead to laugh at the man who lost his sword in the waves, he merely marks the waterline in vain.
Not a thread of silk hangs upon him; yet the bare flesh still remains. Ten thousand miles of cloudless sky, yet the blue heavens still persist.

Even if you look upward and see no heaven, or bend your head and see no earth; even if the path of birds is cut off of all trace and your entire body has no breath to exhale—you would still be falling into the mold of the worldly crowd.
Do you know the one path that transcends this? A straw raincoat and bamboo hat, worn askew; gather them up.
Take up the silk line and return home.
Your true countenance is revealed, yet it still bears traces of rouge and powder. Free yourself from all personal views, lest you fall into the extremes of nihilism or eternalism.

Suddenly, with a shout, disperse the white clouds and burst through the azure void. Upon reaching the gate of the *Qianyuan* (Source of Heaven), you will find yourself unfit for the role of a messenger. Do you understand?
If refined gold is not cast into the furnace, how can its brilliance be brought forth with ultimate clarity?
Zhongqiu said: "The vast multitude gaze upon the Mid-Autumn moon; they needlessly record the seasons of Jambudvīpa.
The wise do not see the bright moon as round before their eyes; it is already like adding more grit to the eye. To blind the eye, one must first remove the grit. Last night, the third...
Turning further toward the west, he startled the azure dragon, causing its horns to snap.
The Master was at Zhengfeng when he again accepted the invitation from Huangbo, saying: "In the depths of spring, I do not let the white ox go idle;
As before, he follows the herd into the wild mountains. Dragging the plow and pulling the harrow to repay past debts, His tail is revealed once more for all to see."
He accepted the invitation from Mount Gu and said: "The National Teacher’s phrase regarding not crossing the stone gate was entrusted before his tongue had even been raised.
How could one bear to engage in conceptual thought upon meeting him face-to-face? A hawk soaring toward the heavens flies off to Silla.

To reveal it in such a manner is already to strike out the five-colored marrow of the phoenix and smash the pearl beneath the jaw of the black dragon. O sharp-witted ones, if you understand the point of return in this way, you have truly seen.
A stroke right under the heels—do you know it? The Great Summit is so high that there is no room for further progress;

the waters of the Spirit-Source are so swift that who would dare to drop their oars? Even if one were to let out a shout that makes the current flow backward, that still would not be considered extraordinary.
Is there anyone who can turn back the pivot of the ultimate gate? After a long silence, he said: "A three-foot Mohe sword lies crosswise in my grasp; I do not know..."
"Who is the one who emerges?

A monk asked, "What is it like when you subtract a little from where there is too much and add a little to where there is too little? The Master said, "It is already pierced through in seven places and perforated in eight.
The monk pressed further, "I do not yet understand the essential meaning within this; I beg the Master for a skillful means to rouse me once more. The Master—
The Master said, "Night travel is not permitted; at first light, you must turn back. The monk said, "Climbing a mountain, one must reach the summit; entering the sea, one must reach the bottom.
The Master said, "This fellow has only just now glimpsed the truth. The monk bowed. The Master then said, "Subtract a little from where there is too much;
the white clouds on the official road are selling private salt. One’s very life is cast away—fear not!"

In the beginning, when Wang Lingyan held the whisk at Xichan Monastery and was appointing monks in the Head Seat’s quarters, he said: "A phrase that does not reveal its wind-bone; before it is even raised, it has already been bestowed. He then took a step forward.
His mouth chattered on and on. Xuan knew he was utterly at a loss. To expose things in such a manner is already like treating a dead horse with medicine;
will you accept it? If you accept it, it is much like mistaking a servant for a lord; if you do not accept it—what then?
Furthermore, this is like cutting off one's own head while seeking to stay alive. When you arrive here, how do you propose to explain it?

A person of sharp faculties—once they see through it with a single glance—need not hesitate to sit in ease. If you are merely traveling along the path, a light pressure is all that is required, and you will immediately see what lies beyond the Iron Ring Mountains.
Yet nowadays, students spend the winter here and the summer there; the Great Dharma remains unclarified.
They have been constantly racing about with their lips and beaks, boasting of their own views and imagining that there is no one in the whole world who can equal them.

Little do they realize that their very lives and natures are entirely in the hands of others. Day and night, their karmic consciousness is in a frantic bustle; when will they ever reach home? Look at those who have reached home:
as soon as they open their mouths and move their tongues, they naturally leave the mud and water behind, bringing life to the eyes of men. When has this ever happened [for the boastful]?
Furthermore, how could this be realized through the mental understanding of the mind’s objective conditions?
Did not Master Deshan show the assembly by saying: "To ask is already a fault; not to ask is still contrary [to the truth]. As soon as a monk stepped forward, Deshan struck him.
The monk said, "The words have not even been asked; why do you strike me? Deshan replied, "I wait for you to open your mouth."
What can it possibly do? The ancients possessed such means; they were like a blazing fire consuming the sky, leaving no room for even a blink of an eye—how could there be any place to draw near?
When some people hear this being said, they instead give rise to interpretations based on the words, claiming, "I am the Dharma King;
I am sovereign over the Dharma. There is no place where you understand, and there is no place where you do not understand. If you act in this way...
Such a view and understanding not only misses the mark regarding Deshan, but also obscures one's own eye for traveling the path. Now, do you wish to take the direct shortcut and meet [the truth]?
Just now, the old man in the abbot’s quarters offered this instruction: An outsider asked the World-Honored One, "I ask neither for words nor for wordlessness.
The World-Honored One remained silent for a long while. The outsider then praised him, saying, "The World-Honored One is most magnanimous and compassionate."
"Dispel the clouds of my delusion and enable me to enter. The Master said, "Listening to matters without clarity, one calls a bell a water jar.
Ānanda continued to ask the World-Honored One, "What have the non-Buddhists realized that they say they have entered? The World-Honored One replied, "They are like fine steeds of the world;
upon seeing the shadow of the whip, they gallop forward. The Master said, "Tell me, where exactly is the place of seeing the shadow of the whip? Later...
Master Xuedou said: "Once the clouds of delusion have cleared, one will certainly see the Buddha. Would you permit that those who study together [be considered as such] or not?
If you all understand this in common, then the masters of the world are all companions of external paths (*tīrthika*).

If each lacks mutual certification, then the patch-robed monks of this land are not as good as the external path practitioners of the Western Heavens. Furthermore, Master Daowei Zhe of Dayu said: "External path practitioners harbor the ultimate..."
The Jewel. The World-Honored One personally held it aloft for Gopati; the myriad phenomena of the universe were clearly revealed.

Furthermore, Ānanda struck the golden bell once more, so that the fourfold assembly could hear it together. Even so, it was much like two dragons contending for a pearl—only strengthening the fierce majesty of the wise.
The Master said: "These two old fellows—one possesses the diamond eye that pierces through the four continents."

One person washes clods of earth in the mud; they have not yet escaped the predicament of being unable to save themselves. If anyone can distinguish between the black and the white, they still cannot escape being left standing there in dullness before the World-Honored One.
Why is this so? Had there been no "blue eyes" and "white eyes" facing one another, how could the wind of the ancestral school have reached the present day?
Eulogy Verse:
At midnight at Huangmei, the Sixth Patriarch mistakenly handed it over; as soon as he got a mere glimmer of it, he began to act recklessly. On the summit of Dayu Ridge, he defecated—
A mound. Descendants of later generations have been defiled by it.
Huangbo’s karmic affinity was not in Beimen Village; when traveling on foot, when had he ever studied under Baizhang? In his dreams, he longed to return to Huangbo.
The Mountain: Without cause, a green cliff rises from level ground.
At Yangyu Hermitage, a water conduit was built;
the path winds around the head of a ten-thousand-fathom precipice. Carrying spring water and wearing the moon, when will it ever cease? Within this, turn the pivot and penetrate the heavens.
The Orifice. People are naturally at ease while the water flows of itself.

By Reverend Yaya of Baitang. On the day of ascending the seat to open the hall, while residing as the successor to Master Lan’an at the Jingshe Monastery in Wenzhou, after the question-and-answer session was concluded, he said: "A sword is suspended in the great void."
To manifest our school: its majestic spiritual power is so formidable, who would dare to compare themselves to it? O clever fellows, as soon as you hear it mentioned, kick it up and go!
You must cut off the heads of both the *nirmāṇakāya* and *saṃbhogakāya* Buddhas; standing directly before you like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.
If you seek the standard within words or clarify the essence beneath a phrase, you are a fox lingering in its den—you will not survive a single pounce. Why? Because this matter cannot be...
It is known by the mind, yet it cannot be attained through a mindless state; it cannot be constructed through language, nor can it be communicated through silent stillness.
It is like the spark struck from flint, resembling a flash of lightning; once the eyes blink, there is no longer any connection.
Therefore, Huangbo struck with the head of his staff and Dayu applied it beneath the ribs; therein lies contraction and expansion, the ability to distinguish and discern. It may be said:
Thus assisting the transformation of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*), one may repay the unrequitable debt of gratitude. May the Way of the Emperor and the Way of the Buddha flourish far and wide;
may the Imperial Wind and the Patriarchal Wind forever waft together. Truly, it is like the wind blowing and the grass bowing, or water reaching and the channel forming.

With the seas calm and the rivers clear, let fishermen’s songs and woodsmen’s chants all together rejoice in this era of peace and prosperity. How would you express this? It is the auspicious vapor of Great Peace.
Boundless Manifestation. Sailing upon the ocean and climbing mountains, he offers prayers for the Sage’s Radiance. Again, it is said:

When Luoshan first entered the world, as he ascended the seat, he merely adjusted his robes, took his place, and immediately said, "Take care. He then added, "Those who have not yet understood, come forward.

"The first arrow strikes the person; the second arrow strikes deep. Since the passing of Master Zhong, few have understood this Way."
He raises the whisk and says: "Do you see it? The great sun floods the eyes; ten thousand miles away, not a single speck of cloud hangs.

Truly, this is rarely heard of in antiquity or today. Haiyin Xin said, "Nothing surpasses this. The Master said, "Before the Most Honored One, what a grand Buddhist service!

Its emergence is like [the thread] from a spool.

He appears but rarely in this world. the nostrils remain as before, mounted upon the upper lip. One simply says that though the person and the moon are the same from year to year, every time they meet, they appear anew.
Whether practicing or making offerings, the horse-master beats the drum to stir windless waves; how can they compete with this night, perfectly full?
A person stands atop the solitary peak of the Wondrous Mountain.
Citing an occasion when Zhaozhou was once informed by an attendant, "The Great King is coming. Zhaozhou said, "Ten thousand blessings to the Great King!
The attendant replied, "He has not yet arrived. Zhaozhou said, "And yet you say he is coming. The Master said: "When he comes, the palace follows him;

"Applying paint here and smearing it there—tell me, how about today? When meeting people, take care not to misquote.

those with merit cultivate and advance ever further upon the basis of merit. It is like the confluence of a hundred rivers returning to the sea, or like adding nine fathoms to complete a mountain.
Splendor follows splendor, and excellence follows excellence. This is the Great Dāna.

Having severed both obstacles and realized both emptinesses, yet desiring to realize Perfect Enlightenment (Pariniṣpanna-bodhi) while not having reached its ultimate limit—this is the domain of the Bodhisattvas. It consists of knowing suffering and severing the origin [of suffering].
The realization of cessation and the cultivation of the path—by means of the sound of the Buddha-way, let all hear it.
This is the matter concerning the five hundred and eighteen great Arhats at Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa. As for the upward path, not a single sage has transmitted it;

Thus shall the descendants of the blue-eyed barbarian be made ever more flourishing. There is a white...

By Imperial Decree: To open the hall at Lingyin Monastery, an imperial messenger was dispatched with an imperial incense offering.

It is fitting to disclose this before the assembly. Holding up the incense, he prays for the Emperor, saying: "This single offering of incense has its spiritual roots flourishing before the seven Buddhas;
its auspicious vapors swirl above the nine heavens. With reverence, I offer it for the longevity of His Majesty the Emperor.
May he reign as a sovereign over the Great Brightness, surveying the world for boundless eons, and be a friend to Heaven and Earth."

At the inception of the Grand Ultimate (*Tàijí*), may the years of your reign be long and the Mandate of Heaven remain steadfast. We respectfully pray that the golden branches and jade leaves of your lineage shall intermingle in radiant splendor like a jeweled net;

and that the ocean of your blessings and the mountain of your longevity shall remain unmoved even as the city of *Sarṣapa* (mustard seeds) is consumed by fire. We also pray for the civil and military officials:

that they may wear their jade pendants and tinkling bells as Heaven brings together the enlightened and the virtuous; and that, climbing the dragon and attaching themselves to the phoenix, they may daily renew their contributions to the governance of the state.
Yes. This single offering of incense cannot be seen with the eyes; it cannot be smelled by the nose. Having endured hardships throughout half a lifetime, it has been obtained easily all at once.

One wishes to transcribe the Dharma transmitted by Bodhidharma; one wishes to record the wondrous realization attained by the present Emperor.
Yet, as for writing, words cannot exhaust it; as for transcribing, the brush cannot reach it.

Precisely at this point where the brush cannot reach and words cannot exhaust—perhaps there may be one or two who pierce through the confusion and perceive the truth with certainty, like a swift falcon darting through the sky, refusing to be caught in a net.
It is like refined gold extracted from ore; it can never change. To know one thing is to know all things;

Your servant is filled with the utmost urgency and trepidation in gazing upon Heaven and longing for the Sage.

[The Master] said, "You have seen it. Master Hao then descended from his seat, and the entire assembly was left bewildered. The Master commented:
"To traverse the realm of one who transcends measure requires the certification of one who transcends measure.

The Four Black Plums: unable to practice Chan and ignorant of letters, they suddenly meet amidst the clamor of the basket; having exhausted the talk of their entire lives, each returns home.
Ten days of rain and five days of wind—their singing and dancing bring joy that is inexhaustible.
I have spoken universally here on this separate peak; there is nothing with which to deliberate with you brothers, nor anything with which to investigate with you brothers.

since you left the monastic groves and have encountered spiritual friends, you have done nothing but investigate and study. For now, set aside all else...
Taking this as the fundamental basis—is that not still an error? You listen to people’s words and take them for actual understanding; that is an error.
Speaking of "mind" and "nature" and taking them for the ultimate principle; that is an error. Taking wordless silence for profound mystery;
that is an error. Taking the striking of staffs and the shouting of "Ho! for rigorous intensity; that is an error. Asking about the east and asking about the west...
To take cleanliness as the goal is a mistake. To take picking up the spoon and grasping the chopsticks as something already accomplished is a mistake.
To take a flash of lightning or a spark from flint as being direct and immediate is a mistake. To take eating when hungry and sleeping when tired as being plain and real is a mistake.
To take being naked as being "home-arrived" is a mistake. To take reviling the Buddhas and scolding the Patriarchs as being one's fundamental duty is a mistake.

If you can let go all at once, cutting it off completely and exhausting it entirely, becoming a true monk whom water cannot wet and wind cannot penetrate, this will not be considered an extraordinary feat.
Should you, however, stubbornly clutch the head of a dead snake, then even if the thousand sages were to appear, there would be no way for them to save you.
Śākyamuni Buddha spent three incalculable eons practicing with diligent hardship.

His every action was solely for this purpose. When, through his extraordinary power of aspiration, he manifested birth in a royal palace, left the home life, and attained enlightenment, he did so merely to serve as an example.

Nowadays, everyone says that the "separate transmission outside the teachings" and the "non-establishment of words and letters" constitute the essential doctrine of Bodhidharma, while everything Śākyamuni preached during his forty-nine years is merely the vehicle of the teachings (śāsana). They do not realize that this old fellow—
He constantly demonstrated this intent, and whenever he encountered a master of the Way, he would invariably bring it forth.
One day, in the city of Rājagṛha, he saw two *caṇḍālas* passing by carrying a pig on a litter. The Buddha pointed to them and asked, "What is this?
The *caṇḍāla* replied, "The Buddha possesses all-encompassing wisdom; yet you do not even recognize a piglet. The Buddha said, "I must ask you about this anyway. Tell me, World-Honored One—"
Where does the meaning lie? You must ask why. On another day, as the assembly gathered for the hall discourse, the World-Honored One did not utter a single word.
Tell me, where does the meaning lie? Herein, it is as firm as a mountain and as deep as the ocean; there is no room for deliberation.

the Dharma-king’s decree is not like this. This is still merely a verdict based on the facts of the case.

At this point, the life of Śākyamuni Buddha was as precarious as a thread hanging from a string. Furthermore, on another day, a non-Buddhist asked:

Once the assembly had gathered for the hall discourse, he said, "Drink tea," and then immediately descended from his seat. At other times, he would say:
"Rest. He would then descend from his seat. At other times he would say, "Take care," and then descend from his seat.
Throughout his life, he frequently used these specific occasions and circumstances, yet people did not understand his intent. This old fellow kills without using a blade;

it is simply because he has a place of genuine realization that he brings it forth. Naturally, this is free from both mud and water. Later, he himself composed a verse on these three turns of the Dharma wheel.
The Record states: "Baizhang had three secrets: 'Tea, take care, and rest. Directly beneath this, one must accept it;

Do you understand? Baizhang was fortunate to have these words, which saved him by half. Later, the Ancient Tower Master said:
"As for Master Heng composing this verse—tell me, what was his realization? Do you know whether he gained or lost?

Ox-head *ābhas* and *yakṣas* and *rākṣasas*, with teeth like sharp swords and mouths like blood-basins, lead various sinners to assemble here.
If one points upward, then the heavens of the Four Dhyānas, the Six Desire Heavens, the Trāyastriṃśa, and the Naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñā—all the devas—appear from the midst of space.
Brahmā, Śakra, celestial sons, and celestial maidens gather here, with celestial music playing everywhere and celestial incense wafting everywhere.

Even so, do you all see them? If you can see them, not only will you be fellow practitioners with the whisk of the Flower Treasury World, but you will also realize the Samādhi of the Play of Supernatural Powers. If it is otherwise, you will not only be left behind.
Huazang’s whisk: Today Huazang has suffered a defeat.

After the Prefect, a member of the Court of Deliberation, and various eminent gentlemen had entered the mountain to pay their respects at the newly constructed Wheel Repository (Lunzang), they requested that he ascend the seat.
A monk asked, "In the past, Zhaozhou received people according to three grades, specifically for the sake of the two kings of Yan and Zhao.
Today, the imperial carriage has entered the mountain; I wonder how you, Master, will receive them? The Master said, "We have already met at the Green Ivy Pavilion."
The monk said, "From ancient times to the present, there has never been a lapse; it is clearly right before one's eyes. The Master asked, "What is that which is right before your eyes?
The monk said, "I have not yet asked about the transgression. The Master said, "You know only the first part, but you do not know the second.
The monk said, "As for the high officials turning the Great Dharma Wheel, I wonder what kind of karmic reward they receive? The Master said, "There is rain that cannot wet them."
"Even without the wind blowing, it is fragrant. The monk said, "Thank you, Master, for your response. The Master said, "After prostrating, withdraw.

The Master then looked toward the assembly and said, "In the past, at the assembly of the Great Parinirvāṇa, the Great Teacher Tathāgata extended his *tūla-cotton* hand, pinched a small amount of earth before the seat, placed it upon his fingernail, and asked Kāśyapa Bodhisattva: 'The earth on my fingernail—'"

"If one were to compare the soil of the great earth with the soil on a fingernail, which would be greater? He replied, "The soil of the great earth is immeasurably vast; the soil on a fingernail cannot be compared to it.

The Buddha said, "It is so. Among all sentient beings in the world, those who obtain a human body from a human body—those who are not born in remote regions, but grow up in wealthy and noble families, endowed with the ten marks of excellence, and whose wisdom encompasses heaven and earth—are as rare as the soil on a fingernail compared to the soil of the great earth."
Discerning the myriad things, one knows how to be loyal to the sovereign, filial to one’s parents, and fraternal toward siblings;

refraining from all evils and practicing all virtues, one reverently places faith in the Triple Gem and carefully guards the three karmas. Drawing near to virtuous friends, one seeks to clarify the mind and realize the fundamental source.
Those who exhaust principle and perfect their nature, thereby transcending birth and death and surpassing the mundane to enter the sacred, are as rare as the dust upon a fingernail.
From losing a human body to receiving the body of a hell-being, a hungry ghost, or an animal, they pass through hundreds and thousands of kalpas.
Furthermore, even if they regain a human body, they will be born in a remote region within a poor and lowly family, lacking the ten physical marks.

They will be foolish and mentally obstructed, not knowing how to be loyal to their sovereign, filial toward their parents, or fraternal toward their brothers. They will commit various evils and fail to practice manifold virtues;

they will not reverently believe in the Triple Gem and will not carefully guard the three karmas of body, speech, and mind. Thus they will wander through the realms of suffering with no time of escape, as described above.
Upon the great earth, when viewed from this perspective, among the three realms and six paths of existence, a human body is the most difficult to obtain.
Having obtained a human body and possessing these numerous virtues while being free from those many evils is even more difficult.
Thus, the Tang Prime Minister Pei Gong said: "Ghosts and spirits suffer the bitterness of deep obscurity; birds and beasts harbor the sorrow of frantic flight."

The asuras are currently in a state of rage, while the devas are immersed in pleasure; it is only by regulating one’s mind and thoughts that one can advance toward Bodhi, and this is possible only through the human path.
If a human being does not do so, there is nothing I can do for them. This is intended to exhort people to study the Buddha-way.
If a person does not study the Buddha-way, they are merely abandoning themselves. Thus, regarding Śākyamuni Tathāgata’s—
The Way is silent and vast; it cannot be grasped through form or name. Subtle and signless, it cannot be known by a conscious mind.
It transcends all existence to ascend into the profound, and it measures the Great Void in its permanence. To speak of its greatness, it encompasses worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges;
to speak of its subtlety, it gathers and condenses everything back into a single minute speck of dust. To speak of its radiance, it outshines the sun and moon.
It is insufficient to compare its brilliance. As for its capacity to cover and sustain all things, even Heaven and Earth cannot rival its virtue.

It can cause growth and development without being spring or summer; it can bring about transformation and decay without being autumn or winter; and it can provide nourishment and moisture without being wind or rain.
It is neither yin nor yang, yet it can bring about transformation and creation. One cannot follow it to its end; one cannot look back at its beginning.

It was born before heaven, yet it does not dwell in its majesty; it ages after heaven, yet it does not claim its longevity. To be deluded by it is to merge with the dust and turn one's back on awakening;
to realize it is to enter the state of sagehood and transcend the mundane. To distance oneself from it is to drift and sink within the sea of suffering; to pursue it...
Then there is the bliss of humans and devas. There is no need for extensive searching through texts; it requires only a single thought-moment of turning the light back upon itself.

If one can simply eliminate all inverted delusions,攀緣 (pān-yuán—clinging to objects), attachments, and the impure mind that pursues birth and death, then in a single kṣaṇa, one will realize the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*). Therefore, the ancients said: "The numinous light shines alone, utterly transcending the sense faculties."
Dust: its substance reveals true permanence; it is not constrained by words and letters. Its nature and characteristics are untainted; it is fundamentally and spontaneously perfected.
Simply by being free from delusive conditions, one is the Buddha of Suchness (*tathatā*). As for the four elements and five aggregates of all people—whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down;
whether conditioned or unconditioned; whether speaking or silent—all are delusive conditions. But tell me, what is the Buddha of Suchness? Do you understand?
The fish lives because its golden scales are released from the girdle; the horse finds relief because the jade bit is loosened for the spring outing.

That which is moist returns to water; that which is dry returns to earth; that which is hot returns to fire; that which moves returns to wind. Thus, the four great elements (*mahābhūta*) cannot be apprehended.
Since the four great elements cannot be apprehended, the four marks of birth, old age, sickness, and death likewise cannot be apprehended. This...

This is called the emptiness of persons (*pudgala-śūnyatā*). Since the past has already ceased, the future has not yet arrived, and the present does not abide, the three periods of time cannot be apprehended.
Once the three periods of time cannot be apprehended, then the ten directions—east, west, south, north, the four intermediate points, above, and below—likewise cannot be apprehended.
This is called the emptiness of phenomena (*dharma-śūnyatā*). If there is one who thoroughly realizes these two types of emptiness, they will immediately awaken to the same awakening as a Buddha.
Even so, Yunmen spoke to the point: "Last year I met the spring;
my rosy countenance reflected the peach and plum blossoms. This year I meet the spring; white hair presses against both ears."
A human life lasts seventy years, as fleeting as an eastward-flowing stream. If one does not realize the original mind, how can one escape birth and death?
(He strikes the whisk. He descends from the seat.
Bending the bow at Stone Gong and setting up the arrow at Xinghua, he wields the strength of Nārāyaṇa and fixes the gaze of Śakra.
He does not shoot the Great Hero-tiger; he does not shoot the Yaoshan-deer; he does not shoot the Yunyan-lion; he does not shoot the Elephant-bone-monkey.
"Tell me, what was he shooting at? After a long silence, he said, "I let this one pass.
A monk asked, "What was the intent behind Bodhidharma’s wall-gazing at Shaolin? The Master said, "He had entered meditative concentration (*samādhi*).
The monk said, "If that is so, then you have failed the ancients. The Master said, "Rarely does one encounter a true connoisseur. The Master then said, "There is a Great Man, a True Gentleman."

Wisdom encircles heaven and earth; eloquence withers the myriad things. One treats the Hundred Schools and Nine Streams as dregs and lees, regarding Yi Yin, the Duke of Zhou, Confucius, and Mencius as mere dust and grime.

Having fully realized one’s own mind and self-nature, and having simultaneously attained the Great Function and the Great Mechanism, one laughs at the pointing at the cypress and the holding up of the flower, and bows loftily to Śākyamuni and Maitreya.
Today, one suddenly halts the reins at the nature-sea of Vairocana and strides freely through the Flower Treasury (Avataṃsaka) Dharma-assembly—how majestic!
A wind that sweeps across the earth has arisen; among the monks of the four seas, who would dare to look upon it with a direct eye?
Even so, when ancients met, the Way was present in their mutual gaze. When the drum is beaten and one ascends the hall, is it not too much of a circumlocution? After a long silence, he said:
"The official seal does not admit even a needle, yet private passage allows for carts and horses."
Blind staffs and blind blows—Linji was not the equal of Deshan. Wild shouts and chaotic shouts—Deshan was not the equal of Linji.

The Miao-yang lineage skillfully transmits the father-son relationship; the Cao-dong school sets up the ruler-minister relationship in a crosswise manner. Yunmen has boundless entanglements; Fayan possesses the same mind-dharma.
All the views of these five houses mentioned above are merely gouging out flesh to create sores. If one were to view them with the correct eye...
Observe this: what kind of monkey’s antics are these? Is there now any monk who can act as a true host for the ancients?
Come forth and meet with Huazang! After a long silence, he said: "A mantis does not refuse the tracks of a chariot;
a firefly dares to burn the mountains."
Birth, old age, sickness, and death—these four gates of affliction cause all sentient beings to suffer greatly in their minds; though they seek to escape them, they cannot do so.
Eternity, bliss, self, and purity—these four gates of liberation cause all sentient beings to take great delight in their minds.

Though they seek entry, they cannot find it. Today at Huazang, I shall borrow this whisk to act as the Great Guide, pointing out the path so that all people may exit through this gate and enter through that gate, uprooting the bitter roots of birth and death and realizing the blissful fruit of Nirvana.
Even so, tell me: where is the beginning of the path? Those with the eye of discernment, try and say!
Look! He drives the sheep-cart to receive the śrāvakas; he drives the deer-cart to receive the pratyekabuddhas; he drives the ox-cart to receive the bodhisattvas.
But tell me, what does he drive to receive the patch-robed monks? A three-legged donkey trots along, prancing its hooves.
Twenty-five [kinds of] perfect penetration; twenty-five equipped with iron shackles; a hundred thousand gates of samādhi; a hundred thousand beams and iron chains.
You great men who have left the household life to travel as mendicants—what is the reason for your attachment?
To take this body born of your parents and shoulder his iron shackles, to wear his iron chains—if you now wish to wander alone through the triple world, you must truly rely upon the Buddha-dharma.
These two words must not be heard with the ears before they can be attained. As the ancients said:
"Even if there were a dharma superior to nirvāṇa, I would say it is like a dream and like an illusion. Nevertheless, you must truly reach this state before you can attain it.
If you have not yet reached this state, do not be careless.

The Lantern Festival. On this auspicious occasion of the First Month’s Full Moon, lanterns are lit throughout the four seas. In the Flower Treasury World (*Huazang*), the Buddha-activity is likewise performed with lamps.
First, the nature-ocean of Vairocana is used as the bowl; next, the supreme merit of the sands of the Ganges is used as the oil;
in the center, unsurpassed Bodhi is used as the wick; and finally, vast wisdom is used as the flame. This lamp, by means of its non-...
It is a point, yet it is a point; therefore, it is eternally a point. It is light, which illuminates by not illuminating; therefore, it is eternally illuminating.
From the Akaniṣṭha Heaven above down to the Avīci Hell below, there is nothing it does not penetrate and nothing it does not clearly perceive.

"Beings of the four modes of birth and the six classes of existence—all sentient beings—upon encountering this lamp-light, shall all recover their original minds and emerge from the shell of ignorance.
Do you all wish to see such a pure, subtle, and inexhaustible lamp? After a long silence, he said: "Burn it through the gateway of the face."
Those who clarify the eye are hindered by the eye; those who awaken to the mind are hindered by the mind; those who realize the Way are hindered by the Way;
those who penetrate the Dharma are hindered by the Dharma. Why is this so? It is said: "Though gold dust is precious, if it falls upon the eye, it becomes a cataract.
If you wish to stride freely across the great square, you must directly eliminate these four hindrances.
A monk asked, "What is the phrase that cuts off all streams? The Master said, "The sluice gate beneath the dam.
He asked, "What is the phrase that follows the waves and drifts with the current? The Master said, "The boatman goes down to Yangzhou. He asked, "What is the phrase that encompasses heaven and earth?
The Master said, "Seamless, it does not allow a breath of wind to pass. He asked, "These are the three phrases of the ancients; what are the phrases of the Master?"
The Master said, "Repeated words should not be swallowed. He then continued: "Forging the Iron Ring Mountains into a fishing hook, With bait suspended for eighty-four thousand oxen.
Casting it idly within the ocean of Vairocana, Shrimp, crabs, fish, and dragons all shrink their heads.
He then raised the following: Formerly, a monk asked Yunmen, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharmakāya? Yunmen said, "North."
"Concealing one's body within a *dou* (peck-measure). The Master said, "What do you call this 'Dharma-body'? You seek yet another phrase to penetrate the Dharma-body.
Such a fellow creates complications upon complications and adds branches to the branches. Fortunately, you encountered the compassion of the ancients;
had it been Huazang, you would have received thirty blows, and not even a single blow could have been spared. Nevertheless—"
The Way. Yunmen speaks thus; what is his intention? Do you wish to understand? A green snake always uses its waist as its feet;
a red amaranth sometimes takes its leaves for flowers.
The Emperor bestowed the title of Master Guangjian upon him and spoke this verse: "Layer upon layer of deep dew falls upon the Azure Garden;
How can this withered and decrepit one repay the Sovereign’s grace? Sitting within a mass of white clouds while burning incense, I illuminate past and present through the Gate of Non-duality.

He further said: "The Way is fundamentally nameless, yet it is forcibly named 'the Way. The Ten Epithets are established in response to conditions; the Three Bodies exist for the sake of [sentient beings]."
Things manifest themselves. Thus, when one engages with principle (*li*), there is only the single void; when one engages with phenomena (*shi*), there is the myriad phenomena arrayed in profusion.
Now, if names are absent, one nearly ceases to function within the Way; if forms exist, they may obscure the Truth.
Yet, if one now wishes to attain a wondrous resonance with one’s own mind, one must simply not involve oneself in the two extremes of name and form or speech. Then, he raised his whisk and said:
If you say it is the whisk, you are stuck in existence with form and name. If you say it is not the whisk, you again fall into non-existence without name or form.
How can one avoid involving oneself in these two extremes? Do you wish to understand?
Three hundred and sixty thousand acres of Taihu Lake—the moon speaks from the heart of the waves; to whom does it speak?
Raising the moon over the Yangtze, the wind blows through the pines. Throughout the long night and clear evening, what is there to do?
If there were someone who could find an entrance here, you may be certain they would be foremost in understanding emptiness.
The north wind is like a blade, piercingly scraping the very bones of men. A thousand mountains, ten thousand mountains, where snow reflects the cold sun.

In my heart, I know the breath of spring is arriving; before my eyes, the plum blossoms have burst forth. Does the traveler returning from the south come back or not? In the quiet hall at dawn, the "tortoise-hair" whisk remains idle.

To exhaustively study the thousands of sutras and myriad treatises is like entering the ocean to count its sands; yet to awaken to the True Eye and the Wondrous Mind is to mistake a thief for one’s own son.
To dwell in non-action and non-activity is to fall into the deep pit of liberation; what difference is there between such diligent and arduous practice and binding oneself with no rope?
Thus the ancients said: "It is not permissible to proceed thus, nor is it permissible not to proceed thus. It is thus...
It is not so; in every way, it is unattainable. Is there now any monk who can hold hands with the Flower Treasury World (Huazang)?
Come forth from the assembly and deliver a message! A strange beast hides its head and horns; a spiritual bird cherishes its feathers and plumage.

To carve patterns into water is merely to exhaust one’s mind and strength; to fashion vessels from empty space is but a waste of effort. Only by roaming the vast ocean can one begin to fathom its depth;
only by ascending Mount Sumeru does one realize its height and distance. Under the gate of the Great Sun, what use is a mere torch?
Beside the scabbard of Mohe, a dull blade may as well be discarded. [He] struck his whisk and descended from the seat.
Having trampled through the illusory city and arrived at the place of treasure, he does not seek the jade of Mount Huai nor probe for the pearl from the dragon’s jaw.
With his tattered robes piled upon his shoulders, he sits idly by the brazier; such a man may be called a "do-nothing practitioner" and is worthy of the offerings of devas and humans.
Huizang’s teaching in this manner is not out of good intentions.
Deshan’s staff fell like a rain of points, and Linji’s shout was like the roll of thunder;

though these sounds shook the world for a time and their elegance has endured for ten thousand generations, upon close examination, they were still merely contrived displays. Huizang does not do it this way: [he stands] within three bays.
In my thatched cottage, beneath the pine gates for ten li, when I am vigorous I stroll freely; when weary, I lie down and sleep soundly.
My body is like withered wood, my mind like extinguished ashes. When someone laughs at me for being foolish, they are simply scratching the very place where I feel an itch.
Vertically, it does not exhaust the three periods of time; horizontally, it does not span the ten directions. Great, yet it does not crowd the void; minute, yet it does not enter a mustard seed.
To the Buddhas of the three ages, it is like awakening or like a dream; to the great patriarchs, they are as if existing or as if gone.
In such a realm, even the holy ones of antiquity were as bewildered and obscured as this. As for practitioners today, how shall you penetrate it?
Dwelling here, must one still seek understanding? Once the snow has melted away, spring will naturally arrive.
Above, the sky is not seen; below, the earth is not seen. With the throat firmly gripped, where can one draw breath? South of the Yangtze, north of the Yangtze.
Cut off by a hair’s breadth, severed by a speck of dust; from the Eastern Land to the Western Heaven, they form a single mass. Even Śākyamuni and Maitreya are still deluded;
how could Linji and Deshan even attempt to deliberate upon them? For the patch-robed monks, there is no handle to grasp—yet they call six pairs "twelve" (a shout).

How strange, O virtuous practitioners of dhyāna! Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra have manifested as Hanshan and Shide. They wear hats made of scorched fat upon their heads and tread in bottomless hempen shoes;
they are clad in coarse cloth tunics smelling of hawk-skin and girded with waistbands of broken leather thongs.
In hand they hold clappers, and from their mouths they sing aloud: "My mind is like the autumn moon, Clear and bright within the azure pool. There is no...
"Things may be compared and matched, but how can I explain it? If Huazang had seen this at the time, he would have given each person a severe beating.
Why so? It was simply to make them dare not act like madmen, lest later generations fall into doubt."
He then took up his staff and said, "Where have you gone? He struck the meditation seat, descended from it, and proclaimed:
"Brandish the sword of wisdom to shatter the net of afflictions; pull out the roots of birth and death and place them within the abode of nirvana.
Empty the lairs of the Mara kings and sweep away the barriers of the evil realms; expand the borders of prajñā and nurture the seed-nature of bodhi."
Acting in this way, establishing oneself in this way—does there still exist any monk whose spirit is not level, who does not grant mutual acknowledgment?
The majestic carriage advances in vain upon its path; who has seen a mantis able to block the ruts?
He raised his fist and said: "The entire Great Canon of teachings, the words and phrases of all the great ancestral masters and the old monks of the world—all are right here.
Even when it is clearly pointed out, people still do not know it. If it is covered over like this, how can one understand it?"
A monk asked, "Are the intent of the Patriarchs and the intent of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, "The Fanfeng is tall; the Jiaoxiao is short.
The monk said, "If that is so, then they are not the same. The Master said, "The Goose-King chooses his own milk; he has never been of the duck species. The Master then said:
Holding a long pole, rowing a short skiff; a single bamboo hat, no second raincoat. The autumn waters of Lake Dongting are not stirred by the wind;
their empty reflection is like a newly polished mirror. This final word is left for Xie Sanlang—*tu!* (a shout of challenge).
The Words of Chan Master Shu’an Yi Ascending the hall, he said:
“When a demon acts as a Buddha, the decaying void originally possesses a skeleton. When a Buddha acts as a demon, clear waves surge atop the summit of Mount Sumeru.
Sitting still in both extremes—neither demon nor Buddha—one does not need donkey-load medicine to cure an illness.”
"Accidentally merging with the water and clouds, yet not being the same as the water and clouds; where the clouds disperse and the water flows, all is silent and the heavens and earth are empty.
When the ancients spoke thus, it was much like Xu Liu carrying a single board. Shui-an, however, is not so:

"Delightedly meeting with the water and clouds, willingly being the same as the water and clouds; where clouds mass and waters gather, they fill up the vast void. Therefore it is said: "A thousand..."
The waves rise in competition; all are the family style of Mañjuśrī. A single expanse of clear sky—nothing is not the bed and couch of Samantabhadra.
To understand it in such a way is precisely the business of novices and junior practitioners. You must know that Zen monks have a distinct excellence of their own.
What is this excellence of the Zen monk? He lets out a shout and strikes the meditation seat.

On the first day of the twelfth month, it is said: "This morning marks the change of the dawn. We humbly beseech the Head Seat, the Great Assembly, the Administrative Officers, and the Heads of Departments to take heed.
'Nine times one, nine times two'—the weather is so cold that hands do not emerge from the sleeves. 'Nine times three, twenty-seven'—by the hedge, the *bibuli* (reed flute) is blown.

'Nine times four, thirty-six'—sleeping at night is like staying out in the open air. Bending and then stretching, expanding and then contracting; throughout the night, ten thousand calculations are made."

A thousand thoughts swirl like a ball of hemp-thread within the breast; one cannot even sleep soundly. When dawn breaks and one rises, the feet tread upon solid ground, yet the head still carries the roof.
If you attempt to deliberate upon this as a matter of Buddha-dharma, your mouth will go dumb and your tongue fall out.
If you treat it as a worldly convention, it is like a hornless cow giving birth to a calf. The whisk says, "I have awakened! I have awakened! I, the mountain monk, say: You!
"What have you awakened to? The whisk said: "Pitiful are those people in the world who pursue evil; six times six is originally thirty-six. Master Yuanwu said:
"When practicing Chan, practice until there is no place to practice; when practicing until there is no practicing, only then do you reach the ultimate end. Cui...
Yun said: "When practicing Chan, practice until there is no place left to practice; practice until even 'no place to practice' has not yet been fully penetrated.
If you wish to exhaust the view from a thousand li, you must go up one more story. He gave a shout.
The黄梅 (huángméi) rains break the summer heat; white milk tea refreshes the spirit. Ten thousand conditions reach him not—this is the life of a wild monk beyond the mundane world.

When Master Fokue arrives, they meet and clasp hands, no longer discussing the mind. The nature of the mind is gold within our own eyes. Three pieces of firewood are smoldering in the shape of a "pin" (品). With you, we idly converse of ancient monasteries.

When the firewood is spent and the night grows deep, [The verse concludes with: The moon is high, the mountain road is long; the old man returns to his hut alone. *Note: The final lines provided in the source text appear to be a continuation of the poetic sequence.*
The bell-chimes from atop the tower fall upon a cold, descending moon. A single tangle of willow filaments cannot be gathered; they are draped with mist against the jade balustrade.

Frozen clouds, on the verge of snowing yet not yet snowing, accompany the majestic elephant-carriage of Samantabhadra. On the ridges, plum blossoms are half-closed and half-opened at Shaoshi Mountain.
When the scenery and light leak forth, and you go on like that, it is still only a partial presentation. What, then, is the full presentation?
Do not speak before those without wisdom; it will break your head and split your brain!
Ascending the hall on the occasion of the Emperor’s Birthday, [the Master] struck once with his staff and said, "Do you hear? He then picked up the staff and said, "Do you see?
With his hand held horizontally across it, he said, "A single branch of spring upon the ten-thousand-year vine; used to celebrate the Ten-Thousand-Wagon Sovereign, the Radiant Yao.
May his person be firm, long-lived, and eternally unaging—a free body in this era of Great Peace."
The swallows depart; the beam is quiet and still. The wild geese arrive; the field of vision is vast and wide. What is there in the courtyard? The wind shakes the bamboos, making a *shanshan* sound.
[The Master] strikes the meditation seat once with his whisk and descends from the seat.
In the ancient verse: "What is the Way? That which is outside the wall. Puhua strikes at the front;
Zhaojue’s house style is not one of deceptive evasion. When asked about the Great Way, he answers, "Chang'an. Who can return home by walking on level ground?
Go! For the most part, you are merely making difficulties for yourself.
With a single squeeze, the silver mountains and iron walls collapse; in the Hall of Great Compassion, the village elders are driven out together.
If Nālada’s staff is of no use, give it to the old man Wanhui, who feigns madness.
The place where he hid his body has vanished without a trace;
Three times he calls for his attendant, yet there is no trace of him to hide, nor anything left to conceal. Entirely free of dependence, they meet face-to-face;
The ancient mirror does not trouble itself to reflect, yet it shines by itself. Thin mist and dew dampen the autumn light.
Three times I call out; you must know my intent is not slight. My lifelong liver and gall are revealed all at once. Do you realize whether you have failed me or failed yourself?
Even with the finest brush and ink, no painter could capture this.

Mount Sumeru. Ciming’s bowl and crosswise sword—without giving rise to a single thought, Mount Sumeru stands tall before you; look directly at it. Seizing a single strand of silk, he lightly trips him over.
At the door of every house, the road is long and peaceful.
The family mountain points out the way; it is not far. Ten-thousand-fathom peaks rise steeply into the azure heavens. A single sheet of white cloud spans the mouth of the valley;
how many returning birds lose their nests!
The old woman throws her child; Yunmen speaks of the falling cliff.
The old woman of Yantou has an iron-hearted mind; she shatters heaven and earth to seek one who can appreciate her sound.
If you do not realize it when your eyebrows are raised, the treacherous waves of Yueyang will grow ever deeper.
Eighteen beauties with graceful and coquettish charms; their embroidered robes light and neat, as a subtle fragrance wafts abroad.
Raising themselves, they stand slowly amidst the flower garden, drawing forth yellow orioles to alight upon the willow branches.
The Words of Master Yun of Biefeng *Successor of Ciyuan Yuan, ascending the hall:* "Our school has no words or phrases, nor does it bestow a single dharma upon others.

Yet, if one were to remain perpetually blocked off in this way, throughout the entire world not a single person would dream of their parents before birth.

This has been so from the very beginning; therefore, following the examples of the former masters of old, and recollecting the power of the skillful means practiced by the Buddhas of the past, they proceeded to strike and circumambulate the second head. A clay-sculpted yakṣa runs through the water; not so, not so. Chewing up a glowing red lump of iron—amidst the "so," it is not so.
Three thousand li beyond the southern flank of Mount Sumeru—amidst the "not so," it is indeed so.
As soon as the "hair-cutting blade" is raised, the Ox and Cow constellations shiver with cold. This is already a failure to recognize good from evil;

If you can entrust yourself to it, then you shall see with the same eye, hear with the same ear, smell with the same nose, and taste with the same tongue as all the Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past.
The same bodily contact, the same mental intention—there is no further distinction. That is to say: it is thus with every dust mote, thus with every land, thus with every thought-moment.

Winter night. In our school, there are no words or phrases, nor is there a single dharma given to others. Furthermore, even if we were to instruct the senior monk who holds the whisk, how could he possibly open his mouth here?

The "Peach Pit of a Thousand Years. Later, Master Yuan held it up and said: "A peach pit of a thousand years has sprouted shoots;

A "large sweet melon" is another name for a pummelo. It is like chestnuts, mustard seeds, or hemp seeds; like peach blossoms, apricot blossoms, or plum blossoms—there is indeed such fortune.
Olives from the province; there are also papayas from Xuanzhou and local "ox-heart" persimmons from Sichuan, along with honey-soaked kōng shoots.

however, please leave the seeds for this mountain monk to plant as seed next year. Great and small, far and near.
The Master said: "I picked up a single peach pit and grew a few small, miscellaneous fruits.
I did not store them away, but brought them all out at once to satisfy my hunger. This can truly be called 'knowing how to enjoy oneself regardless of one's wealth.
Where does elegance lie? Not in wearing many garments. Even on a cold winter night, I have some fruit; this is quite different from other places. It is not like Zheng."

Zhou-li pears, Qingzhou dates, Weishan persimmons, Xuefeng tangerines, Hanshan bitter peaches, the acorns and chestnuts from the wooden rack, and the crabapples from Lingyun Forest—these are the plum of Damei.
Fragrant things are fragrant; sweet things are sweet; sour things are sour; and astringent things are astringent.

This also shows that there was someone within the assembly who did not see Deshan’s Way: "Here there is no Buddha and no Patriarch;

"Perfect Enlightenment" and "Sublime Enlightenment" are merely the breaking of attachments by ordinary people; "Bodhi" and "Nirvana" are but hitching posts for donkeys;

One day, suddenly buffeted by the winds of karma, you find yourself cast upon a crooked wooden bed; then you say, "I am of the Linji lineage," and "You are of the Yunmen lineage.
You categorize the schools and divide the branches, causing a flurry of disputes. Is this not, indeed, to do injustice to the ancients? I, this mountain monk, [say this].

Furthermore, why do you stay outside the gate? This mountain monk has never, with you all, gone so far as to pick up Newara and Champaka to have them butt heads within the eye of a gnat.

there is birth and there is killing. In the illumination of the sun and moon, there is light and there is darkness; there is concealment and there is manifestation.
