Glory and decline have their thanks; the seasons shift in succession. There is going and there is coming; there is new and there is old. As for the old:

at every gate they crackle firecrackers, and in every place they bid farewell to the year. As for the new: when the green trees have barely changed their leaves, the red buds already burst into bloom.
[The Master] then gave a shout and said: "Tell me, is this new or is it old? If you cannot discern it, on the thirtieth day of the twelfth month—"
Today there is a matter of great importance. For this reason, the Old Man with the Yellow Face said:

"All sentient beings continue in the cycle of birth and death because they do not know the eternally abiding true mind, the essence of pure and luminous nature. They employ various deluded thoughts; these thoughts are not real."

Therefore, there is cyclic existence (*saṃsāra*). If people wish to ensure that birth and death do not continue and that false conceptualization (*vikalpa*) does not arise, they must directly recognize this eternally abiding true mind, the essence of pure and luminous nature; only then can it be attained. Is there anyone here present who recognizes it right now?
Consider, for instance, how spring brings forth and summer causes growth, autumn wanes and winter declines, as heat passes and cold arrives, welcoming the new and seeing off the old. Furthermore...
What is this? Before one’s eyes, lamps and candles shine brightly; sitting and standing are solemn and still; questions and answers fly back and forth;
host and guest stand in mutual opposition. Where, then, do all you people come and go? If you understand it here, then you have understood.

You must not harbor a thought or stir a single mental movement, for then there is no connection. Without harboring thoughts and without stirring the mind, each and every thing is authentically true; each and every thing is luminously wondrous.
To speak in such a manner—under the gate of the Patriarchs, this is called "a dead snake blocking the main road.

Tonight, this mountain monk, braving the ridicule of all quarters, wishes merely to respond to the occasion. If you are a liberated practitioner, upon meeting others you must cast away the object used for knocking at the door;
once the path is found, you must forget even the name of the milestone. Thus, naturally, in all places, you will not be obstructed by dharmas.
Bound. Not seeking liberation through the Dharma. Amidst the frequent tolling of the clear sounding-stone, one is beyond right and wrong; a solitary idler within heaven and earth.
If you practice by clinging to the Dharma, you are like an ox pulling a millstone. After thirty years, do not mistakenly blame others.
Studying Chan must result in awakening; otherwise, one’s learning will ultimately remain muddled and superficial. Before those with the clear eye, you cannot deceive them by even a single point.
How would you describe the principle of awakening? Is it that "the nun was originally a woman"?
Is it that "heaven and earth share the same root with me, and the myriad things are one body with me"? Is it that "it is luminously clear"?

"At the tip of every blade of grass—how clearly manifest is the meaning of the Patriarchs! Is it not like seeing smoke from a mountain and immediately knowing there is fire, or seeing a horn over a wall and immediately knowing it is an ox?

The boiling cauldrons and glowing coals are right there. Even if you look upward and see not a single speck of dust or a Buddha, look downward and see not a single being in the six realms or four modes of birth;

if internally there is no mind that can realize and externally there is no dharma that can be realized—naked and bare, stark and clear—if you let go and arrive home, people will not recognize you. Having nothing at all to offer the Honored Hall, it is like avoiding drowning.
And yet he threw [the ox] into the fire. How can one provide a theoretical explanation for this? Can one avoid the fault of harming the object? Nanquan said:

If you lead the ox westward toward the stream, you likewise cannot avoid infringing upon the King's water and grass. It is better to simply accept things as they are; even so, nothing is seen. Now, there is only this.
Letting go from emptiness, I spread it out equally with all people. Last night, atop the summit of Mount Sumeru, a clap of thunder resounded;
the Dragon King Sāgara was startled awake in his dreams, mounted backward upon a carp of the Eastern Sea, and poured down a great rain within the pores of a lotus fiber.
It pervaded the entire world without exception, until the servant of Kunlun ran off toward Tiantai.
In the mountains he gathered acorns and chestnuts, until his entire body was soaked through;
he performed several somersaults in succession and leapt onto the top of a *huabiao* pillar, sitting there with his feet upturned. He waited for the sun to rise in the east to dry his iron trousers.
Only the mounting platform before the gate remained dry and parched before him, nearly causing a great disaster. *Jin* (The Golden).
Gang and the deity Shen-sha fought one another for an entire night. One said, "The dry side is right! The other said, "The wet side is right! Another said, "Both are right!
Still another said, "Both are not right! One said, "Let the dry side remain dry; let the wet side remain wet.
The mountain monk then gave a shout and said, "In the middle of the night, why are you quarreling over a hot bowl here? He took up his staff and drove them all away at once. However—

Thus, for those of superior capacity, whatever is required is employed; their transformative ingenuity is boundless, and they grant or withhold according to the occasion. Their unfolding and withdrawing rest entirely within themselves.
It is like throwing a sword into the empty sky—one cannot debate whether it reaches its mark or not—and moreover, it is free from deliberation.

They do not concern themselves with tonal prosody or parallelism, as seen in such lines as "A single wild goose in autumn across the Milky Way" or "A thousand households with mortars and pestles at night. This is how one must achieve a sharp and novel response to the task at hand.

[This concludes] the Verse on the Ancient Case.

The Buddha ordered Ānanda to go and ask him: "Are you at peace in hell? Devadatta replied: "Though I am in hell, it is as pleasant as dwelling in the Third Dhyāna Heaven.

The Buddha again ordered [Ānanda] to go and ask: "Do you still seek to leave? Devadatta replied: "I shall wait for the World-Honored One to enter, and then I will immediately leave. Ānanda said: "The World-Honored One..."

"This is the entrance into the Dharma-gate of non-duality. Mañjuśrī asked Vimalakīrti again, but Vimalakīrti remained silent.
Mañjuśrī exclaimed, "Excellent, excellent! Even to the point where there are no words or speech—this is the true entrance into the Dharma-gate of non-duality."

Zhunyu said, "It has passed. Zhaozhou said, "It hits the mark."

The Master cited a case for the assembly’s further inquiry, saying: "A monk asked Zhaozhou, 'The myriad dharmas all return to the One;

The Master held up the staff and said: "A vast capacity rests in the palm; it possesses the majesty of Pushan (Guliang) parting Mount Taihua. A clear mirror stands upon its stand;

The monk said, "Master, do not let the sound of a boiling bowl ring out like excrement. Touzi then struck him.

The strength to uproot Mounts with a tripod; the black steed *Wuwei* could not easily be ridden even for a thousand li.

Where white clouds part, the bright moon is seen; when yellow leaves fall, the sound of pounding clothes is heard. I urge you: if you wish to rest, then rest at once;
if you seek the moment of completion, there will be no time of completion.
Singing alone with fresh clarity, the rhythm differs from the common; Spacious and vast through the ages, its meaning is inexhaustible.
If you intend to open your eyes to listen before the sound, You have already been carried away by the wind into another tune.
The Fifth Patriarch, the Venerable Master, cited the monk’s question to Zhaozhou: “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?

What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The cypress tree in the courtyard. Only when you understand it in this way is it finally so.
The *Jiaren* hexagram transforms into *Mingyi*. The lines and images are clear and need no further inference. Without action and without scheming, there will ultimately be auspicious celebration;

The World-Honored One’s appearance emerging from the mountain:

All day long you carry a leather bag and run through the streets; though you have a mouth, when have you ever recited the *Lotus Sūtra*?
At the end, your empty fabrications are even more intolerable—Jetavana will not tolerate your further additions.
The Elder Anāthapiṇḍada: Master Yunmen went far to welcome Gautama to Anāthapiṇḍada’s Grove;

he stood waiting to hear the Dharma so it might be revealed. Had he known early on that this Dharma required renunciation, he would have gladly requested [the Buddha] to depart for the capital at that very moment.
Zhongdu of Muzhou and Shen-yuan of Xueqiao: uprooting has no gate, carving emptiness to make an aperture. There is the calamity of a broken leg;
this is the omen of a ruined house. Master Wanfu, may you tolerate this unworthy one.
Seeing Master Zizhi off as he departs the mountains for various regions:

No one speaks there, and you have nothing to hear. When both hearing and speaking are absent, do not stumble at the heels. As soon as you give rise to even a hair’s breadth of a thought regarding something extraordinary, you remain, as before, unable to step out from beneath the thunder-gate.
